concepts.label: Refrain
concepts.definition: A recurring line or musical passage, often returning within or at the end of successive verses.
concepts.note: Line repeated at the end of each verse.

concepts.label: Bridge
concepts.definition: A contrasting song section that departs from established verse or chorus material before returning to it.
concepts.note: Contrasting section, usually once, before the last chorus.

concepts.label: Interlude
concepts.definition: A short passage inserted between larger sections, often instrumental or transitional in character.
concepts.note: Instrumental or transitional section between parts.

concepts.label: Instrumental break
concepts.definition: A passage in which instruments take over while the principal vocal part pauses.
concepts.note: Passage without vocals.

concepts.label: Solo section
concepts.definition: A passage that foregrounds one performer or instrument, often for melodic invention, improvisation, or technical display.
concepts.note: Showcase section for an instrument.

concepts.label: Guitar solo
concepts.definition: A passage featuring guitar as the principal melodic voice, whether improvised, composed, acoustic, or electric.
concepts.note: Electric or acoustic guitar solo.

concepts.label: Saxophone solo
concepts.definition: A passage in which saxophone takes the leading melodic role, often supported by a rhythm section or ensemble.

concepts.label: Piano solo
concepts.definition: A passage featuring piano in the leading role, either unaccompanied or supported by other instruments.

concepts.label: Synth solo
concepts.definition: A passage foregrounding a synthesizer lead, often using distinctive timbres, pitch bends, or melodic runs.

concepts.label: Bass solo
concepts.definition: A passage featuring bass as the main musical voice, emphasizing melodic, rhythmic, or harmonic possibilities beyond accompaniment.

concepts.label: Breakdown (metal)
concepts.definition: A heavy, rhythmically focused section in metal or hardcore, often using slower-feeling grooves, rests, and repeated low-register riffs.
concepts.note: Slow, heavy section of syncopated muted chords.

concepts.label: Breakdown (EDM)
concepts.definition: A lower-intensity section in electronic dance music that reduces or removes the main beat before rebuilding energy.
concepts.note: Low-energy section without kick before the build.

concepts.label: Build-up
concepts.definition: A passage that increases tension through rising intensity, added layers, repetition, or denser rhythmic activity before a release.
concepts.note: Progressive rise in tension before the drop.

concepts.label: Drop
concepts.definition: A high-impact section in electronic dance music where the principal beat, bass, or hook enters or returns after a buildup or break.
concepts.note: Climax of an electronic track, where bass and kick come in.

concepts.label: Beat switch
concepts.definition: A deliberate change of the underlying beat or production within a track, often marking a new section or expressive direction.
concepts.note: Complete change of beat mid-track; hip hop.

concepts.label: Hook (hip hop)
concepts.definition: The recurring hook section of a hip-hop track, often functioning as a chorus between verses.
concepts.note: The chorus of a rap track.

concepts.label: Skit
concepts.definition: A brief spoken scene, comic passage, or narrative vignette included within a song or between tracks on an album.
concepts.note: Spoken piece or short scene on a hip hop record.

concepts.label: Spoken intro
concepts.definition: A spoken opening that introduces a track, establishes a narrative, or sets an atmosphere before the main musical section.
concepts.note: Recited opening before the music.

concepts.label: Final chorus
concepts.definition: The last occurrence of a song's chorus, often varied or intensified to provide a climactic finish.
concepts.note: Last chorus, often intensified or doubled.

concepts.label: Turnaround
concepts.definition: A short harmonic passage that leads from the end of a section back to its beginning or into the next repetition.
concepts.note: Chord passage leading back to the top of the form.

concepts.label: Tag ending
concepts.definition: A short ending extension that repeats or varies a final phrase, line, or chord pattern.
concepts.note: Final repetition of the last line.

concepts.label: Outro
concepts.definition: The closing section of a piece, providing a final statement, resolution, or gradual departure from the main material.
concepts.note: Closing section.

concepts.label: Fade-out
concepts.definition: A recording or performance ending in which the sound level gradually decreases until it becomes inaudible.
concepts.note: The song ends by gradually lowering the volume.

concepts.label: Cold ending
concepts.definition: A clear, abrupt ending achieved through a final note, chord, hit, or cutoff rather than a gradual fade.
concepts.note: Ending on a hit, no fade.

concepts.label: False ending
concepts.definition: A moment that appears to end the music before it resumes, creating surprise or renewed momentum.
concepts.note: Pause that fakes the ending before the music returns.

concepts.label: A cappella section
concepts.definition: A passage performed by voices without instrumental accompaniment, even if the surrounding music uses instruments.
concepts.note: Voices-only passage.

concepts.label: Dramatic pause
concepts.definition: A deliberate interruption of all sounding parts, used to create tension, emphasis, or a sharp structural contrast.
concepts.note: Brief total silence for impact.

concepts.label: Song forms
concepts.definition: The overall organization of a song into repeated and contrasting sections, such as verses, choruses, and bridges.
concepts.note: Overall organizational schemes.

concepts.label: Verse–chorus form
concepts.definition: A song structure built around alternating verses and recurring choruses, sometimes including an introduction, bridge, and outro.
concepts.note: Alternating verses and choruses with an optional bridge.

concepts.label: AABA form
concepts.definition: A four-section form in which two related A sections are followed by a contrasting B section and a return of A.
concepts.note: Form of the Tin Pan Alley standards.

concepts.label: Strophic form
concepts.definition: A form that uses the same music for successive verses or stanzas of text.
concepts.note: Same music for every verse.

concepts.label: Through-composed form
concepts.definition: A form in which new musical material follows the text or narrative instead of relying on a regularly repeating sectional pattern.
concepts.note: No repeated sections.

concepts.label: Binary form
concepts.definition: A musical form organized into two principal sections, often labeled A and B and commonly repeated.
concepts.note: Two contrasting sections.

concepts.label: Ternary form
concepts.definition: A three-part form with an opening section, contrasting middle section, and return of the opening material.
concepts.note: Statement, contrast and return.

concepts.label: EDM arrangement
concepts.definition: A dance-oriented arrangement that organizes energy through introductions, buildups, drops, breakdowns, and an ending; exact sequences vary.
concepts.note: Intro–build–drop–breakdown–build–drop–outro.

concepts.label: Multi-part epic
concepts.definition: An extended composition joining several contrasting sections or movements into a larger continuous or linked work.
concepts.note: Long composition with linked movements; progressive rock.

concepts.label: Loop-based form
concepts.definition: A structure created by repeating musical loops while adding, removing, or transforming layers over time.
concepts.note: Structure built by adding and removing layers over a loop.

concepts.label: Medley
concepts.definition: A piece or performance that joins recognizable portions of several existing songs or compositions.
concepts.note: Chain of fragments from several songs.

concepts.label: Reprise
concepts.definition: A return of previously heard musical material, often later in a composition, performance, or album.
concepts.note: Return of an earlier theme at the end of a record or work.

concepts.label: Segue
concepts.definition: A transition from one musical passage or track into another without a significant break.
concepts.note: Seamless transition from one piece to the next.

concepts.label: Compositional forms
concepts.definition: A recognized framework or type of composition associated with particular structural, performance, or historical conventions.
concepts.note: Forms of the art-music tradition, aligned with LCGFT.

concepts.label: Fugue
concepts.definition: A contrapuntal composition in which a principal subject enters successively in different voices and is developed through imitation.
concepts.note: Contrapuntal form based on imitation of a subject.

concepts.label: Canon
concepts.definition: A contrapuntal technique in which one part strictly follows another after a delay, sometimes at a different pitch level.
concepts.note: Strict imitation of one voice by another after a delay.

concepts.label: Round
concepts.definition: A repeating canon in which several performers begin the same melody at different times, usually at the same pitch level.
concepts.note: Canon at the unison that repeats indefinitely.

concepts.label: Invention
concepts.definition: A short contrapuntal keyboard composition, commonly in two parts, that develops a small amount of musical material.
concepts.note: Short contrapuntal piece in two or three voices.

concepts.label: Sonata form
concepts.definition: A large-scale form typically involving exposition, development, and recapitulation, with thematic and tonal contrasts shaping its design.
concepts.note: Exposition, development and recapitulation of two themes.

concepts.label: Theme and variations
concepts.definition: A form presenting a theme followed by successive versions that alter its melody, harmony, rhythm, texture, or instrumentation.
concepts.note: A theme followed by successive transformations.

concepts.label: Passacaglia
concepts.definition: A composition built from continuing variations over a recurring bass line or harmonic pattern.
concepts.note: Variations over a repeated bass or progression.

concepts.label: Rondo
concepts.definition: A form in which a recurring principal section alternates with contrasting episodes.
concepts.note: Instrumental refrain alternating with episodes.

concepts.label: Toccata
concepts.definition: A composition emphasizing fluency, rapid passagework, or touch, most often associated with keyboard instruments.
concepts.note: Virtuosic keyboard piece with fast figuration.

concepts.label: Prelude
concepts.definition: A short introductory piece or an independent composition, often freely structured and designed to establish a musical mood.
concepts.note: Introductory or short free-form piece.

concepts.label: Étude
concepts.definition: A composition designed to develop or demonstrate a particular performance technique, sometimes also intended for concert presentation.
concepts.note: Piece focused on a technical difficulty.

concepts.label: Nocturne
concepts.definition: A composition associated with nighttime atmosphere, often lyrical and especially common in the piano repertory.
concepts.note: Lyrical, night-themed piano piece.

concepts.label: March
concepts.definition: A composition with a regular walking or marching pulse, commonly in duple meter and often associated with ceremonial or military use.
concepts.note: Piece in 2/4 or 4/4 at a military pace.

concepts.label: Waltz
concepts.definition: A dance or composition in triple meter, typically with a strong first beat and lighter accompanying beats.
concepts.note: Dance in 3/4 accented on beat one.

concepts.label: Minuet
concepts.definition: A courtly dance and musical form in triple meter, later used as a movement in instrumental works.
concepts.note: Courtly dance in 3/4.

concepts.label: Scherzo
concepts.definition: A lively, often playful or sharply contrasting movement, frequently in triple meter and commonly found in larger instrumental works.
concepts.note: Fast, playful movement in 3/4.

concepts.label: Aria
concepts.definition: A self-contained vocal piece for a solo singer, often expressing emotion within an opera, oratorio, or cantata.
concepts.note: Lyrical solo vocal piece within a larger work.

concepts.label: Recitative
concepts.definition: A vocal style that follows the inflections and rhythm of speech to convey dialogue or advance a dramatic narrative.
concepts.note: Declaimed singing that follows speech rhythm.

concepts.label: Chorale
concepts.definition: A hymn tune associated with Protestant, especially Lutheran, worship, or a composition based on such a tune.
concepts.note: Lutheran hymn harmonized in four parts.

concepts.label: Motet
concepts.definition: A vocal composition, often sacred and polyphonic, whose musical form and text conventions vary across historical periods.
concepts.note: Sacred polyphonic choral composition.

concepts.label: Madrigal
concepts.definition: A secular vocal composition, especially associated with Renaissance and early Baroque traditions, often using expressive musical treatment of poetry.
concepts.note: Secular polyphonic vocal composition of the Renaissance.

concepts.label: Mass
concepts.definition: A musical setting of texts from the Christian Mass, especially its Ordinary, written for voices with or without instruments.
concepts.note: Music for the Ordinary of the Mass.

concepts.label: Requiem
concepts.definition: A musical setting of the Mass for the dead, or a composition inspired by its texts and memorial function.

concepts.label: Hymn
concepts.definition: A song of praise or devotion, commonly intended for communal singing in a religious setting.
concepts.note: Strophic song of praise.

concepts.label: Anthem
concepts.definition: A song or choral work serving a communal, ceremonial, religious, or symbolic purpose; the term has several historical meanings.
concepts.note: Solemn, collective piece; by extension, a mass sing-along song.

concepts.label: Lullaby
concepts.definition: A gentle song or instrumental piece intended to soothe, especially to help a child fall asleep.
concepts.note: Soft song for sleep.

concepts.label: Lament
concepts.definition: A musical expression of grief, mourning, loss, or complaint, found in many vocal and instrumental traditions.
concepts.note: Piece of mourning or grievance.

concepts.label: Serenade
concepts.definition: A composition traditionally associated with evening performance or an affectionate address, later also used for multi-movement instrumental works.
concepts.note: Amorous or light piece, originally performed at night.

concepts.label: Ballad
concepts.definition: A song type associated with storytelling or, in modern popular music, a lyrical and often slower-paced expression of emotion.
concepts.note: Song that tells a story; in pop, a slow song.

concepts.label: Power ballad
concepts.definition: A popular-music ballad that develops from a restrained opening into an intense arrangement with prominent drums and amplified instruments.
concepts.note: Ballad that builds to a finale with full-power guitars and drums.

concepts.label: Rhapsody
concepts.definition: A freely organized, often contrasting or episodic composition with an expressive or improvisatory character.
concepts.note: Free, episodic piece.

concepts.label: Fantasia
concepts.definition: A composition with a free or imaginative structure, often drawing on improvisatory gestures or loosely connected musical ideas.
concepts.note: Free piece with an improvisatory character.

concepts.label: Cadenza
concepts.definition: A featured solo passage, often virtuosic and rhythmically flexible, inserted into or near the close of a larger movement.
concepts.note: Free, virtuosic solo passage.

concepts.label: Overture
concepts.definition: An instrumental opening to an opera, play, or other larger work, also used for independent concert pieces.
concepts.note: Introductory orchestral piece.

concepts.label: Suite
concepts.definition: A collection of related movements or pieces presented as a larger work, historically often based on a sequence of dances.
concepts.note: Series of linked pieces or dances.

concepts.label: Concerto
concepts.definition: A composition that features one or more soloists in a prominent relationship with an orchestra or other ensemble.
concepts.note: Work for soloist and orchestra.

concepts.label: Symphony
concepts.definition: An extended orchestral composition, commonly organized into several movements with contrasting tempos and characters.
concepts.note: Orchestral work in several movements.

concepts.label: Cantata
concepts.definition: A vocal composition in several sections or movements, typically involving soloists, choir, and instrumental accompaniment.
concepts.note: Vocal work in several movements.

concepts.label: Oratorio
concepts.definition: A substantial dramatic work for voices and instruments, usually performed without the staging, costumes, or acting of an opera.
concepts.note: Dramatic choral-orchestral work without staging.

concepts.label: Opera
concepts.definition: A theatrical work in which music and singing play a central role in presenting characters and drama, sometimes alongside spoken dialogue.
concepts.note: Staged drama sung throughout.

concepts.label: Jazz standard
concepts.definition: A composition widely recognized and repeatedly performed in the jazz repertory, often used as a framework for improvisation.
concepts.note: Repertoire tune used for improvisation.

concepts.label: Texture
concepts.definition: The way melodic, harmonic, and rhythmic parts combine, including their density, independence, and relationships.
concepts.note: How simultaneous lines combine.

concepts.label: Monophony
concepts.definition: A texture consisting of one melodic line without independent harmonic accompaniment, whether performed by one or several musicians.
concepts.note: A single unaccompanied melodic line.

concepts.label: Homophony
concepts.definition: A texture in which parts move together harmonically or a principal melody is supported by chordal accompaniment.
concepts.note: Main melody with chordal accompaniment.

concepts.label: Polyphony
concepts.definition: A texture containing two or more simultaneously sounding melodic parts with some degree of independence.
concepts.note: Several independent simultaneous lines.

concepts.label: Heterophony
concepts.definition: A texture in which performers simultaneously produce different versions or embellishments of the same underlying melody.
concepts.note: Simultaneous variants of the same melody.

concepts.label: Unison
concepts.definition: The simultaneous performance of the same pitch or melodic line by multiple voices or instruments.
concepts.note: Several voices or instruments on the same pitch.

concepts.label: Sparse texture
concepts.definition: A musical texture with relatively few simultaneous sounds, leaving audible space between or around its parts.
concepts.note: Few elements at a time, lots of space.

concepts.label: Dense texture
concepts.definition: A musical texture containing many simultaneous or closely packed layers, voices, or events.
concepts.note: Many simultaneous layers.

concepts.label: Counterpoint
concepts.definition: The combination of independent melodic lines according to relationships of rhythm, pitch, consonance, and voice leading.
concepts.note: Combining independent lines under voice-leading rules.

concepts.label: Imitation
concepts.definition: The repetition of a musical idea in another voice or part, often beginning at a different time or pitch.
concepts.note: One voice repeats another's material.

concepts.label: Voice leading
concepts.definition: The movement of individual musical lines from one note or chord to the next, shaping continuity and harmonic connection.
concepts.note: How each voice moves between chords.

concepts.label: Hocket
concepts.definition: A technique in which a melodic or rhythmic line is distributed between parts through alternating notes and rests.
concepts.note: A melody split note by note between voices.

concepts.label: Accompaniment textures
concepts.definition: A pattern or arrangement that supports a principal melody through chords, bass movement, rhythmic figures, or sustained sounds.
concepts.note: Typical accompaniment patterns.

concepts.label: Comping
concepts.definition: Rhythmic and harmonic accompaniment, especially in jazz, using chords and figures that respond to or support a soloist.
concepts.note: Rhythmic, irregular chords under a soloist.

concepts.label: Alberti bass
concepts.definition: A repeated broken-chord accompaniment pattern, commonly ordered lowest-highest-middle-highest.
concepts.note: Broken chord in low-high-middle-high order.

concepts.label: Harmonized lines
concepts.definition: Melodic lines performed together at different pitches, often maintaining parallel or coordinated harmonic intervals.
concepts.note: Two instruments play the same line a third or sixth apart.

concepts.label: Drone
concepts.definition: A sustained or regularly repeated pitch or chord that provides a stable foundation beneath changing musical material.
concepts.note: Note or chord sustained throughout the piece.

concepts.label: Call and response
concepts.definition: A musical exchange in which one phrase is answered by another performer, group, or instrumental part.
concepts.note: Alternation between a solo phrase and a reply.

concepts.label: Antiphony
concepts.definition: Alternating musical passages between two performers or groups, often choirs, in a responsive or spatially separated arrangement.
concepts.note: Alternation between two choirs or groups.

concepts.label: Layering
concepts.definition: The combination or progressive addition of musical parts to build texture, intensity, or contrast.
concepts.note: Elements entering progressively and stacking up.

concepts.label: Voice types
concepts.definition: A category describing a singing voice by range, tessitura, timbre, or performance role.
concepts.note: Voice classification by range and ensemble.

concepts.label: Male vocals
concepts.definition: Vocals performed by male singers; the descriptor does not specify a particular pitch range, technique, or timbre.

concepts.label: Female vocals
concepts.definition: Vocals performed by female singers; the descriptor does not specify a particular pitch range, technique, or timbre.

concepts.label: Duet
concepts.definition: A performance or composition for two principal performers; here, it describes two vocalists singing together or in alternation.
concepts.note: Two singers alternating or singing together.

concepts.label: Soprano
concepts.definition: A high singing voice type, with classifications determined by comfortable range, timbre, and repertoire rather than pitch limits alone.
concepts.note: Highest female voice.

concepts.label: Mezzo-soprano
concepts.definition: A voice type between soprano and contralto, often characterized by a comparatively warm middle register.

concepts.label: Contralto
concepts.definition: A low voice type conventionally classified among female singing voices, known for a rich lower register.
concepts.note: Lowest female voice.

concepts.label: Countertenor
concepts.definition: A voice type conventionally associated with male singers performing in an alto or similar high range, often using a developed head or falsetto register.
concepts.note: Male voice in the alto range.

concepts.label: Tenor
concepts.definition: A relatively high voice type conventionally classified among male singing voices.
concepts.note: High male voice.

concepts.label: Baritone
concepts.definition: A voice type conventionally positioned between tenor and bass, often with a strong middle and lower register.
concepts.note: Middle male voice.

concepts.label: Bass voice
concepts.definition: A low voice type conventionally classified among male singing voices.
concepts.note: Lowest male voice.

concepts.label: Child voice
concepts.definition: A singing voice associated with a child before or during vocal maturation; its range and timbre vary by singer.

concepts.label: Choir
concepts.definition: An organized group of singers performing together, commonly divided into coordinated vocal parts.
concepts.note: Large vocal ensemble.

concepts.label: Gospel choir
concepts.definition: A choir performing gospel-oriented music, often using expressive harmonies, rhythmic emphasis, and exchanges between soloist and ensemble.
concepts.note: Gospel-style choir with handclaps and call and response.

concepts.label: Gang vocals
concepts.definition: A group vocal sound created by several performers shouting or singing together, often loosely in unison.
concepts.note: Several voices shouting in unison; punk and hardcore.

concepts.label: Chant
concepts.definition: A vocal delivery based on repeated or sustained melodic formulas, often with a narrow pitch range and ritual or communal function.
concepts.note: Collective singing recited on few notes.

concepts.label: Singing techniques
concepts.definition: A method of coordinating breath, phonation, resonance, and articulation to produce a particular sung sound.
concepts.note: Techniques of sung vocal production.

concepts.label: Chest voice
concepts.definition: A vocal-register and resonance term commonly used for a full, speech-like singing quality, especially in lower and middle ranges.
concepts.note: Low, resonant register.

concepts.label: Head voice
concepts.definition: A vocal-register and resonance term commonly used for a lighter or higher singing quality; its precise meaning varies among teaching traditions.
concepts.note: High, light register.

concepts.label: Falsetto
concepts.definition: A vocal production commonly associated with a light upper register and relatively thin vocal-fold vibration, often contrasting with a fuller modal voice.
concepts.note: High, airy register above the natural voice.

concepts.label: Belting
concepts.definition: A powerful, speech-like singing quality used at relatively high pitches, shaped by specific resonance and vocal coordination.
concepts.note: Chest register pushed high with great power.

concepts.label: Mixed voice
concepts.definition: A pedagogical term for vocal coordination that combines or balances qualities associated with chest and head registers.
concepts.note: Blend of chest and head.

concepts.label: Vocal vibrato
concepts.definition: A regular oscillation around a sung pitch, contributing to vocal color, expressiveness, and sustained-note shaping.
concepts.note: Periodic pitch oscillation.

concepts.label: Breathy vocals
concepts.definition: A vocal sound with audible airflow alongside the pitched tone, producing a soft or airy quality.
concepts.note: Delivery with lots of air.

concepts.label: Whisper
concepts.definition: A vocal sound produced with turbulent airflow rather than the regular vocal-fold vibration of ordinary voiced speech or singing.
concepts.note: Voice without vocal-fold vibration.

concepts.label: Vocal fry
concepts.definition: A low, creaky vocal register characterized by irregular, relatively slow vocal-fold pulses.
concepts.note: Crackly delivery in the lowest register.

concepts.label: Raspy vocals
concepts.definition: A vocal timbre with audible roughness or distortion; several different vocal mechanisms can produce this quality.
concepts.note: Light, rough distortion; rock and soul.

concepts.label: Twang
concepts.definition: A bright, concentrated vocal quality associated with particular resonance adjustments, often heard in country and other contemporary styles.
concepts.note: Bright, nasal timbre; country.

concepts.label: Yodel
concepts.definition: A singing technique involving rapid alternation between contrasting vocal registers, often across wide pitch intervals.
concepts.note: Rapid jumps between chest voice and falsetto.

concepts.label: Vocal hiccup
concepts.definition: A brief catch, break, or clipped transition in the voice used as an expressive effect, especially in rockabilly-oriented singing.
concepts.note: Clipped breaks in the voice; rockabilly.

concepts.label: Crooning
concepts.definition: A restrained, intimate singing style associated with microphone use and smooth phrasing rather than forceful acoustic projection.
concepts.note: Soft singing close to the microphone.

concepts.label: Operatic singing
concepts.definition: A singing approach associated with opera, emphasizing sustained breath support, resonance, expressive phrasing, and projection.
concepts.note: Classical technique projecting without a microphone.

concepts.label: Melismatic singing
concepts.definition: A vocal style that frequently places multiple notes on individual syllables of text.
concepts.note: Style rich in melismas.

concepts.label: Vocal runs
concepts.definition: Rapid sequences of sung notes used to embellish a syllable or phrase, often featuring scales, arpeggios, or patterned turns.
concepts.note: Fast passages of notes on one syllable; R&B and gospel.

concepts.label: Cante jondo
concepts.definition: A category of flamenco singing associated with profound expression and particular traditional styles; its meaning extends beyond a single vocal technique.
concepts.note: Melismatic, raw flamenco singing.

concepts.label: Overtone singing
concepts.definition: A vocal technique that emphasizes selected overtones so that a sustained fundamental and a higher melodic tone can be heard together.
concepts.note: One voice producing a note and its overtones at once.

concepts.label: Humming
concepts.definition: Vocalizing with the mouth closed or nearly closed, creating a resonant tone without articulated lyrics.
concepts.note: Singing with the mouth closed.

concepts.label: Whistling
concepts.definition: Producing pitched sounds by directing air through a small opening, allowing melodies to be performed without vocal-fold phonation.
concepts.note: Whistled melody.

concepts.label: Vocalise
concepts.definition: A vocal exercise or composition sung on vowels or other nonlexical sounds rather than a conventional text.
concepts.note: Singing on vowels without text.

concepts.label: Scat singing
concepts.definition: A jazz vocal approach using improvised syllables and melodic phrases in place of fixed lyrics.
concepts.note: Vocal improvisation with nonsense syllables; jazz.

concepts.label: Ululation
concepts.definition: A high, wavering vocal sound produced through rapid tongue or mouth movement, used in celebration, ritual, or expressive performance in several traditions.
concepts.note: High tongue trill, typical of North Africa and the Middle East.

concepts.label: Harsh vocals
concepts.definition: A broad descriptor for rough, distorted, or aggressively textured vocal techniques, especially in metal and hardcore.
concepts.note: Distorted vocal techniques of metal and hardcore.

concepts.label: Growl
concepts.definition: A low, rough or guttural vocal sound commonly associated with death metal and related styles.
concepts.note: Low guttural voice of death metal.

concepts.label: Scream
concepts.definition: A forceful, rough, often high-intensity vocal sound used as an expressive technique in several rock and metal styles.
concepts.note: Mid-to-high distorted scream.

concepts.label: Fry scream
concepts.definition: A distorted scream described in contemporary vocal practice as using fry-like coordination; terminology and underlying mechanisms vary.
concepts.note: High scream based on vocal fry.

concepts.label: False chord scream
concepts.definition: A harsh vocal technique commonly described as involving the false vocal folds or other supraglottic structures; the term refers to folds, not musical chords.
concepts.note: Scream using the false vocal folds.

concepts.label: Shriek
concepts.definition: A piercing, high-register harsh vocal sound often associated with black metal.
concepts.note: High shriek of black metal.

concepts.label: Pig squeal
concepts.definition: A harsh vocal effect with a strongly resonant, squealing quality, commonly heard in some deathcore and brutal death metal.
concepts.note: High, pig-like guttural of deathcore and slam.

concepts.label: Clean vocals
concepts.definition: Sung vocals without the deliberately harsh distortion associated with growls or screams; the term is especially common in metal.
concepts.note: Undistorted singing, in contrast to harsh vocals.

concepts.label: Shouted vocals
concepts.definition: A forceful vocal delivery resembling shouted speech, emphasizing intensity and rhythmic attack more than sustained melodic precision.
concepts.note: Shouted, non-guttural voice; punk and hardcore.

concepts.label: Spoken and rapped vocals
concepts.definition: A vocal delivery centered on speech-like articulation and rhythm rather than conventional sustained singing.
concepts.note: Non-sung vocal delivery.

concepts.label: Spoken word
concepts.definition: Spoken text presented as a performance, here used with or within music rather than primarily sung.
concepts.note: Spoken text over music.

concepts.label: Sprechgesang
concepts.definition: A family of vocal approaches between speech and song, in which pitch and spoken inflection are combined in varying proportions.
concepts.note: Technique halfway between speech and song.

concepts.label: Rap
concepts.definition: A rhythmic vocal delivery organized through phrasing, rhyme, accent, and verbal flow, often performed over a beat.
concepts.note: Rhythmic, rhymed delivery.

concepts.label: Flow
concepts.definition: The rhythmic organization and delivery of rap, including syllable placement, accents, phrasing, and interaction with the beat.
concepts.note: Rhythmic pattern of a rap delivery.

concepts.label: Double-time rap
concepts.definition: A rap delivery using approximately twice the perceived rate of syllables or rhythmic activity relative to the underlying groove.
concepts.note: Rap at double the apparent speed.

concepts.label: Triplet flow
concepts.definition: A rap delivery that organizes syllables into three-part subdivisions or repeating triplet-based rhythmic patterns.
concepts.note: Rap in eighth-note triplets.

concepts.label: Melodic rap
concepts.definition: A vocal approach combining rap phrasing with pronounced melodic pitches or sung passages.
concepts.note: Rap with a melodic contour, often with autotune.

concepts.label: Mumble delivery
concepts.definition: A loosely defined delivery descriptor for relaxed or indistinct articulation in some contemporary rap; usage is contested and stylistically broad.
concepts.note: Relaxed, loosely articulated diction.

concepts.label: Toasting
concepts.definition: A Jamaican vocal practice of rhythmic speech, chanting, or melodic interjections over a riddim, influential in later rap and dancehall.
concepts.note: Jamaican rhythmic chanting over riddims.

concepts.label: Beatboxing
concepts.definition: The imitation or creation of percussion and other musical sounds using the mouth, lips, tongue, and voice.
concepts.note: Percussion imitated with the mouth.

concepts.label: Vocal arrangement
concepts.definition: The organization of lead and supporting voices, including their harmonies, entries, textures, and relationships.
concepts.note: Arrangement of voices on the recording.

concepts.label: Lead vocal
concepts.definition: The principal sung or spoken vocal part that carries the main melody, text, or narrative of a recording or performance.

concepts.label: Backing vocals
concepts.definition: Vocal parts that support the lead through harmony, responses, repeated phrases, or additional texture.

concepts.label: Vocal harmonies
concepts.definition: Two or more vocal parts sounding together at different pitches to create chordal or contrapuntal relationships.
concepts.note: Several voices at different pitches.

concepts.label: Close harmony
concepts.definition: A vocal arrangement in which chord tones are placed relatively close together, often within a compact register.
concepts.note: Tightly voiced parts; doo-wop, barbershop.

concepts.label: Double-tracked vocals
concepts.definition: A vocal sound created by recording and combining two performances of the same part, adding thickness and small timing or pitch differences.
concepts.note: The same vocal take recorded twice.

concepts.label: Ad-libs
concepts.definition: Short vocal additions, responses, or embellishments that supplement the principal part, whether improvised or planned.
concepts.note: Spontaneous vocal interjections.

concepts.label: A cappella
concepts.definition: Vocal music performed without instrumental accompaniment, although voices may imitate instrumental or percussion sounds.
concepts.note: Voices without instrumental accompaniment.

concepts.label: Vocal call and response
concepts.definition: A vocal exchange in which a soloist or group presents a phrase and another voice or group answers it.
concepts.note: Soloist and choir alternating.

concepts.label: Plucked strings
concepts.definition: String instruments whose sound is primarily initiated by plucking, whether with fingers, a plectrum, or another mechanism.

concepts.label: Guitar
concepts.definition: A fretted plucked string instrument with a long neck and a flat-fronted body, usually with six strings, in acoustic and electric forms.
concepts.note: General term; use the narrower terms when the type of guitar is known.

concepts.label: Acoustic guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar whose hollow body projects string vibrations acoustically, with steel-string and nylon-string designs among its common types.

concepts.label: Classical guitar
concepts.definition: A nylon-string acoustic guitar associated with classical repertory and fingerstyle playing, typically using a wide fingerboard.

concepts.label: Flamenco guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar built and played for flamenco, typically favoring a quick response, bright attack, and techniques such as rasgueado and picado.

concepts.label: Archtop guitar
concepts.definition: A steel-string guitar with an arched top and f-holes, often fitted with pickups, long the standard rhythm and solo guitar of swing and jazz.

concepts.label: Electric guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar whose string vibrations are converted into electrical signals by pickups, allowing amplification and extensive sound processing.

concepts.label: Clean electric guitar
concepts.definition: An electric-guitar sound with little audible clipping or distortion, preserving a relatively clear attack and pitch definition.
concepts.note: Undistorted sound.

concepts.label: Distorted guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar sound altered by clipping or saturation, adding harmonics, sustain, compression, and a rougher timbre.

concepts.label: Electric sitar
concepts.definition: An electric guitar with a special buzzing bridge, and often sympathetic strings, built to imitate the timbre of the sitar.
concepts.note: An electric guitar fitted to imitate the sitar, not a sitar.

concepts.label: Twelve-string guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar with six paired courses of strings, commonly combining unison and octave pairs for a rich, shimmering sound.

concepts.label: Extended-range guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar with additional strings or an expanded pitch range beyond the common six-string design; this concept includes seven-string and other extended-range instruments.
concepts.note: Guitars with added low strings; modern metal.

concepts.label: Steel guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar played with a steel bar pressed on the strings instead of fretting, giving sliding pitches and sustained tones.
concepts.note: Guitars played with a steel bar rather than by fretting; general term.

concepts.label: Pedal steel guitar
concepts.definition: A steel guitar played horizontally, with pedals and knee levers that change string pitches while a bar stops the strings.

concepts.label: Lap steel guitar
concepts.definition: A steel guitar played horizontally on the lap or on legs, with a steel bar sliding along the strings, typical of Hawaiian and steel-guitar gospel music.
concepts.note: Played flat on the lap or on legs; for resonator instruments use Resonator guitar.

concepts.label: Resonator guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar with one or more metal resonator cones that amplify the strings acoustically, played with a slide or lap-style with a steel.
concepts.note: Played lap-style or held like a guitar with a slide.

concepts.label: Baritone guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar with a longer scale tuned lower than a standard guitar, typically a fourth or a fifth below.
concepts.note: Longer scale and lower tuning than a standard guitar; not the same as an extended-range guitar.

concepts.label: Vietnamese guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar with scalloped frets that allow pitch bends and ornaments, the lead of cải lương.

concepts.label: Viola caipira
concepts.definition: A Brazilian ten-string guitar in five courses, the instrument of rural music of the center-south and the northeast.

concepts.label: Electric bass
concepts.definition: A low-register amplified string instrument, commonly played with fingers or a pick to provide rhythmic and harmonic support.

concepts.label: Fretless bass
concepts.definition: A bass instrument without fixed frets, allowing continuous pitch movement and flexible intonation along the fingerboard.

concepts.label: Double bass
concepts.definition: A large, low-register bowed string instrument, also widely plucked in jazz and other styles to provide bass lines.

concepts.label: Banjo
concepts.definition: A plucked string instrument with strings stretched over a membrane-covered resonating body, producing a bright, percussive sound.

concepts.label: Tenor banjo
concepts.definition: A four-string banjo with a short neck, usually tuned in fifths, used for chordal rhythm in early jazz and for melody in Irish traditional music.

concepts.label: Mandolin
concepts.definition: A small plucked lute-family instrument, commonly with four paired string courses tuned in fifths.

concepts.label: Ukulele
concepts.definition: A small plucked string instrument associated with Hawai'i, usually having four strings and a bright, compact sound.

concepts.label: Lute
concepts.definition: A family of plucked string instruments with a neck and resonating body, including the European lute and related regional instruments.

concepts.label: Harp
concepts.definition: A plucked string instrument with strings running at an angle to its soundboard, typically offering separate strings for different pitches.

concepts.label: Sitar
concepts.definition: A long-necked plucked string instrument associated with Hindustani music, featuring movable frets and sympathetic strings.

concepts.label: Oud
concepts.definition: A short-necked, fretless plucked lute widely used in Middle Eastern and neighboring musical traditions.

concepts.label: Bouzouki
concepts.definition: A long-necked plucked string instrument associated with Greek music, with related adaptations used in other traditions.

concepts.label: Baglamas
concepts.definition: A small Greek long-necked lute, an octave above the bouzouki, used in rebetiko and laiko.

concepts.label: Charango
concepts.definition: A small Andean plucked string instrument, commonly with five paired string courses and a bright upper-register sound.

concepts.label: Cavaquinho
concepts.definition: A small four-string plucked instrument used in Portuguese and Brazilian traditions, especially as rhythmic accompaniment in samba and choro.
concepts.note: Small four-string guitar of samba and choro.

concepts.label: Kora
concepts.definition: A West African plucked bridge-harp, commonly with twenty-one strings, associated with Mandinka and related hereditary musician traditions.
concepts.note: 21-string harp-lute of the Mandinka griots.

concepts.label: Cuatro
concepts.definition: A small four- or five-course guitar-like instrument of Venezuela, Puerto Rico and the Caribbean, with tunings and string layouts that vary by country.
concepts.note: The Venezuelan, Puerto Rican and related cuatros; for the Cuban tres use Tres.

concepts.label: Tres
concepts.definition: The Cuban three-course guitar, with doubled strings, whose syncopated melodic patterns are central to son and related styles.

concepts.label: Koto
concepts.definition: A Japanese plucked zither with movable bridges, traditionally played with finger picks.

concepts.label: Shamisen
concepts.definition: A Japanese three-string plucked instrument with a skin-covered body, commonly played using a large plectrum.

concepts.label: Guzheng
concepts.definition: A Chinese plucked zither with movable bridges, allowing melodic playing, pitch bends, and resonant accompaniment.

concepts.label: Balalaika
concepts.definition: A Russian plucked string instrument with a triangular body, commonly built in several sizes for ensemble use.

concepts.label: Saz
concepts.definition: A name applied to long-necked plucked lutes in Turkish and related traditions, especially instruments of the bağlama family.
concepts.note: Long-necked lute of Turkey and Anatolia.

concepts.label: Sarod
concepts.definition: A fretless plucked lute of Hindustani music with a skin-covered body, a metal fingerboard and sympathetic strings.

concepts.label: Tanpura
concepts.definition: A long-necked fretless lute whose open strings are plucked in a continuous cycle to provide the drone in Indian classical music.

concepts.label: Pipa
concepts.definition: A Chinese pear-shaped plucked lute with four strings and many frets, played with the fingernails or picks.

concepts.label: Gayageum
concepts.definition: A Korean plucked zither with movable bridges, traditionally with twelve silk strings.

concepts.label: Đàn tranh
concepts.definition: A Vietnamese plucked zither with movable bridges and steel strings.

concepts.label: Đàn bầu
concepts.definition: A Vietnamese one-string zither whose harmonics are bent in pitch with a flexible rod.
concepts.note: One-string zither whose pitch is bent with a flexible rod.

concepts.label: Appalachian dulcimer
concepts.definition: A fretted zither of the Appalachian region, usually with three or four strings, played on the lap by plucking or strumming.
concepts.note: Fretted plucked zither; not the hammered dulcimer.

concepts.label: Musical bow
concepts.definition: A string instrument made of a bent stick and a single string, often with a gourd or the player's mouth as resonator.

concepts.label: Berimbau
concepts.definition: A Brazilian musical bow with a gourd resonator, struck with a stick, that leads the music of capoeira.

concepts.label: Hammered dulcimer
concepts.definition: A zither with strings stretched over a trapezoidal soundboard and struck with small hammers.
concepts.note: Struck with hammers, not plucked; listed here with the other zithers.

concepts.label: Santur
concepts.definition: The hammered dulcimer of Iran and Iraq, with many courses of metal strings struck with light hammers.

concepts.label: Santoor
concepts.definition: The Indian hammered dulcimer, adapted from the Kashmiri santoor for Hindustani classical music.

concepts.label: Yangqin
concepts.definition: The Chinese hammered dulcimer, struck with bamboo beaters.

concepts.label: Cimbalom
concepts.definition: A large hammered dulcimer of Central and Eastern Europe, the concert form having legs and a damper pedal, prominent in Hungarian and Romani music.

concepts.label: Khim
concepts.definition: The hammered dulcimer of Thailand and Cambodia, struck with soft bamboo beaters.

concepts.label: Bajo sexto
concepts.definition: A large Mexican guitar with six double courses of strings, providing bass and harmony in norteño and Tejano music.

concepts.label: Portuguese guitar
concepts.definition: A pear-shaped plucked string instrument with six double courses of steel strings, the lead instrument of fado.

concepts.label: Tar (lute)
concepts.definition: A long-necked lute with a double-bowl body covered by a thin membrane, central to the classical music of Iran and Azerbaijan.
concepts.note: The long-necked lute; the North African frame drum also called tar is a different instrument.

concepts.label: Ngoni
concepts.definition: A West African plucked lute with a wooden body covered in skin, played by griots and in Malian popular music.

concepts.label: Kamalen ngoni
concepts.definition: A Malian harp-lute with six to twelve strings, derived from the hunter's harp, central to Wassoulou music.

concepts.label: Kantele
concepts.definition: A Finnish and Karelian plucked zither, from small five-string instruments to large concert models with many strings.

concepts.label: Autoharp
concepts.definition: A zither fitted with chord bars that damp all strings except those of the selected chord, so that strumming sounds a single chord.

concepts.label: Bandurria
concepts.definition: A Spanish and Filipino plucked instrument with six double courses, played with a plectrum, often in tremolo.

concepts.label: Biwa
concepts.definition: A Japanese short-necked fretted lute played with a large plectrum, used in court music and narrative song.

concepts.label: Heike biwa
concepts.definition: The biwa used to accompany the chanted Tale of the Heike.

concepts.label: Doshpuluur
concepts.definition: A Tuvan long-necked lute with two or three strings, plucked or strummed to accompany throat singing.

concepts.label: Dutar
concepts.definition: A long-necked two-string lute of Iran and Central Asia.

concepts.label: Geomungo
concepts.definition: A Korean six-string zither with frets, plucked with a bamboo stick.

concepts.label: Gimbri
concepts.definition: A three-string bass lute with a camel-skin body, the central instrument of Gnawa music.

concepts.label: Guqin
concepts.definition: A Chinese seven-string fretless zither, the instrument of the scholar class, played with harmonics and slides.

concepts.label: Kacapi
concepts.definition: A Sundanese boat-shaped or box zither with many strings, accompanying sung poetry and suling.

concepts.label: Qanun
concepts.definition: A trapezoidal plucked zither of the Arab and Turkish world, with small levers to adjust microtonal tuning.

concepts.label: Krar
concepts.definition: A five- or six-string bowl lyre of Ethiopia and Eritrea, plucked or strummed.

concepts.label: Laúd
concepts.definition: A Spanish and Cuban plucked instrument with six double courses, played with a plectrum.

concepts.label: Octavina
concepts.definition: A Philippine guitar-shaped instrument with fourteen strings in courses, the tenor of the rondalla.

concepts.label: Sanshin
concepts.definition: The Okinawan three-string lute with a snakeskin body.

concepts.label: Sanxian
concepts.definition: A Chinese long-necked fretless lute with three strings and a snakeskin body.

concepts.label: Setar
concepts.definition: A Persian long-necked lute with four strings, plucked with the index fingernail; intimate and soft.

concepts.label: Tanbur
concepts.definition: A family of long-necked fretted lutes of Turkey, Iran and Central Asia.

concepts.label: Tiple
concepts.definition: A small Colombian guitar with twelve strings in four triple courses, the core of Andean Colombian music.

concepts.label: Topshuur
concepts.definition: A two-string lute of the Altai and western Mongolia, accompanying epic singing.

concepts.label: Đàn nguyệt
concepts.definition: A Vietnamese two-string moon-shaped lute with high frets.

concepts.label: Bowed strings
concepts.definition: String instruments primarily sounded by drawing a bow across their strings, producing sustained tones and varied articulations.

concepts.label: Violin
concepts.definition: A high-register bowed string instrument, usually with four strings tuned in fifths, used in classical, folk, and many other styles.

concepts.label: Electric violin
concepts.definition: A violin with pickups, often with a solid or skeletal body, played through amplification and effects.

concepts.label: Fiddle
concepts.definition: A name for the violin in many folk and popular traditions, emphasizing repertory and playing style rather than a separate basic instrument design.
concepts.note: Violin in folk, country and Celtic styles.

concepts.label: Hardanger fiddle
concepts.definition: A Norwegian folk fiddle with sympathetic strings under the fingerboard and a decorated body.

concepts.label: Viola da gamba
concepts.definition: A fretted bowed string instrument of the Renaissance and Baroque, held between or on the legs and bowed underhand.

concepts.label: Sarangi
concepts.definition: A short-necked bowed lute of North India and Pakistan with a skin-covered body and many sympathetic strings.

concepts.label: Viola
concepts.definition: A bowed string instrument larger and lower-pitched than the violin, typically tuned C-G-D-A.

concepts.label: Cello
concepts.definition: A bowed string instrument played upright between the knees, with a resonant range extending from bass to high melodic registers.

concepts.label: String section
concepts.definition: A group of bowed string players within an ensemble, commonly including violins, violas, cellos, and double basses.

concepts.label: Erhu
concepts.definition: A Chinese two-string bowed fiddle, typically played vertically with the bow hair passing between its strings.

concepts.label: Hurdy-gurdy
concepts.definition: A string instrument sounded by a crank-driven wheel, with a keyboard changing melody pitches and additional strings often providing drones.

concepts.label: Nyckelharpa
concepts.definition: A Swedish bowed keyed fiddle in which keys stop the melody strings and sympathetic strings add resonance.

concepts.label: Morin khuur
concepts.definition: A Mongolian two-string bowed instrument with a trapezoidal body and a scroll carved as a horse's head.

concepts.label: Kamancheh
concepts.definition: A spike fiddle of Iran and neighboring regions, with a small round body covered in skin, held upright and bowed.

concepts.label: Rebab
concepts.definition: A name for several bowed lutes with few strings and often a skin-covered body, found from North Africa and the Middle East to Indonesia.
concepts.note: Name shared by several related bowed lutes; use with the tradition in view.

concepts.label: Classical kemençe
concepts.definition: A small pear-shaped three-string bowed lute of Ottoman classical music, held upright on the knee.

concepts.label: Joza
concepts.definition: An Iraqi spike fiddle with a coconut-shell body, part of the chalghi ensemble of Iraqi maqam.

concepts.label: Ghijak
concepts.definition: A Central Asian spike fiddle with a round body, used in Uzbek, Tajik, Uyghur and Turkmen music.

concepts.label: Haegeum
concepts.definition: A Korean two-string fiddle bowed between the strings, used in court and folk music.

concepts.label: Igil
concepts.definition: A Tuvan two-string bowed instrument held upright, often accompanying throat singing.

concepts.label: Saw duang
concepts.definition: A high-pitched Thai two-string fiddle with a hardwood tube body.

concepts.label: Saw u
concepts.definition: A low-pitched Thai two-string fiddle with a coconut-shell body.

concepts.label: Đàn nhị
concepts.definition: A Vietnamese two-string fiddle with a small tube body.

concepts.label: Woodwinds
concepts.definition: A family of wind instruments that generate sound through an edge or reed, regardless of whether their bodies are made of wood or metal.

concepts.label: Flute
concepts.definition: A wind instrument sounded by directing air across an edge or opening, including transverse and end-blown designs.

concepts.label: Piccolo
concepts.definition: A small transverse flute that typically sounds an octave above the concert flute, producing a bright, penetrating upper register.

concepts.label: Recorder
concepts.definition: A duct flute with a whistle-like mouthpiece and finger holes, built in several sizes and commonly used in early music and education.

concepts.label: Tin whistle
concepts.definition: A small six-hole duct flute associated particularly with Irish and other folk traditions.

concepts.label: Pan flute
concepts.definition: A wind instrument made from a row or bundle of pipes of different lengths, each producing a different pitch.

concepts.label: Siku
concepts.definition: Andean panpipes in two rows of tubes, traditionally divided between two players who alternate notes to form one melody.
concepts.note: Andean panpipes, often split between two players who alternate notes.

concepts.label: Quena
concepts.definition: An Andean end-blown flute of cane or wood with a notch cut into the blowing end.

concepts.label: Bansuri
concepts.definition: A bamboo transverse flute of North India, used in classical, folk and film music.

concepts.label: Dizi
concepts.definition: A Chinese transverse flute whose buzzing membrane over an extra hole gives a bright, reedy tone.

concepts.label: Ocarina
concepts.definition: A vessel flute, usually of clay, with finger holes on a closed, rounded body.

concepts.label: Kaval
concepts.definition: A chromatic end-blown flute of the Balkans and Anatolia, held obliquely and known for its breathy tone.

concepts.label: Fife
concepts.definition: A small, high-pitched transverse flute, usually without keys, played with drums in military and folk music.

concepts.label: Shakuhachi
concepts.definition: A Japanese end-blown bamboo flute known for breathy tone colors and flexible pitch and articulation.

concepts.label: Ney
concepts.definition: An end-blown reed flute used in several Middle Eastern traditions, with regional differences in construction and playing technique.

concepts.label: Duduk
concepts.definition: An Armenian double-reed wind instrument with a warm, resonant tone, often made from apricot wood.

concepts.label: Clarinet
concepts.definition: A single-reed woodwind instrument with a cylindrical bore, built in several sizes and valued for its wide range and contrasting registers.

concepts.label: Bass clarinet
concepts.definition: A clarinet pitched an octave below the B-flat clarinet, with an upturned bell and a dark, rich low register.

concepts.label: Oboe
concepts.definition: A double-reed woodwind instrument with a conical bore and a clear, focused tone.

concepts.label: Bassoon
concepts.definition: A low-register double-reed woodwind instrument with a folded conical bore and a distinctive resonant timbre.

concepts.label: Saxophone
concepts.definition: A single-reed woodwind instrument with a conical metal body, built in a family of sizes and widely used in jazz and popular music.

concepts.label: Alto saxophone
concepts.definition: A saxophone pitched in E-flat, occupying a middle-to-high register within the saxophone family.

concepts.label: Tenor saxophone
concepts.definition: A saxophone pitched in B-flat, larger and lower in register than the alto saxophone.

concepts.label: Baritone saxophone
concepts.definition: A low-register saxophone pitched in E-flat, commonly providing bass support or a robust solo voice in ensembles.

concepts.label: Soprano saxophone
concepts.definition: A high-register saxophone pitched in B-flat, commonly built in straight or curved forms.

concepts.label: Zurna
concepts.definition: A loud conical double-reed wind instrument of Turkey, the Balkans, the Middle East and Central Asia, usually paired with a large drum.

concepts.label: Shawm
concepts.definition: A loud conical double-reed wind instrument of medieval and Renaissance Europe, a forerunner of the oboe.

concepts.label: Suona
concepts.definition: A loud Chinese double-reed wind instrument with a conical wooden body and a metal bell.

concepts.label: Sheng
concepts.definition: A Chinese free-reed mouth organ with vertical pipes, able to play chords.

concepts.label: Bagpipes
concepts.definition: A family of reed instruments supplied with continuous air from a bag, often combining a melody chanter with one or more drones.

concepts.label: Great Highland bagpipe
concepts.definition: The Scottish bagpipe, blown by mouth, with a chanter of nine notes and three drones.

concepts.label: Uilleann pipes
concepts.definition: The Irish bagpipe, filled by a bellows under the arm, with a chanter of about two octaves, drones and keyed regulators that can add chords.

concepts.label: Gaida
concepts.definition: A bagpipe of the Balkans and southeastern Europe, made of goat or sheep skin, with one chanter and one drone.

concepts.label: Galician gaita
concepts.definition: The bagpipe of Galicia, mouth-blown, with a conical chanter and one to three drones.

concepts.label: Didgeridoo
concepts.definition: A long drone aerophone developed in Aboriginal Australian traditions, played through lip vibration and often circular breathing.
concepts.note: Australian Aboriginal drone aerophone.

concepts.label: Harmonica
concepts.definition: A free-reed mouth instrument sounded by blowing and drawing air, with pitch and expression shaped by breath and mouth position.

concepts.label: Arghul
concepts.definition: An Egyptian double clarinet of cane with one melody pipe and one longer drone pipe, played with circular breathing.

concepts.label: Daegeum
concepts.definition: A large Korean bamboo transverse flute with a buzzing membrane, used in court and folk music.

concepts.label: Flabiol
concepts.definition: A small Catalan duct flute played with one hand while the other beats a small drum, opening the sardana.

concepts.label: Hichiriki
concepts.definition: A short Japanese double-reed pipe with a penetrating tone that carries the melody in gagaku.

concepts.label: Kagurabue
concepts.definition: A Japanese six-hole bamboo transverse flute used in Shinto kagura music.

concepts.label: Khaen
concepts.definition: A Lao and northeast Thai free-reed mouth organ of bamboo pipes in two rows, played with chords and drones.

concepts.label: Kèn bầu
concepts.definition: A Vietnamese double-reed wind instrument with a gourd-shaped bell, used in court and theater music.

concepts.label: Mijwiz
concepts.definition: A Levantine double clarinet of two cane pipes played together with circular breathing, the lead of dabke.

concepts.label: Nadaswaram
concepts.definition: A long South Indian double-reed wind instrument, played with the thavil drum in temples and weddings.

concepts.label: Nōkan
concepts.definition: The high, piercing Japanese transverse flute of noh and kabuki.

concepts.label: Pi nai
concepts.definition: A Thai quadruple-reed oboe with a bulging body that leads the piphat ensemble.

concepts.label: Piri
concepts.definition: A Korean cylindrical double-reed pipe with a large reed, leading court and folk ensembles.

concepts.label: Ryūteki
concepts.definition: The Japanese bamboo transverse flute of gagaku.

concepts.label: Saluang
concepts.definition: A Minangkabau bamboo end-blown flute played with circular breathing to accompany sung verses.

concepts.label: Shinobue
concepts.definition: A Japanese high bamboo transverse flute used in festival and folk music.

concepts.label: Shō
concepts.definition: A Japanese free-reed mouth organ of seventeen bamboo pipes that plays sustained clusters in gagaku.

concepts.label: Suling
concepts.definition: An Indonesian bamboo ring flute, used in gamelan, kacapi suling and popular music.

concepts.label: Tenora
concepts.definition: A Catalan tenor shawm with keys and a metal bell, the lyrical lead voice of the cobla.

concepts.label: Tible
concepts.definition: A Catalan treble shawm with keys, used in the cobla.

concepts.label: Whistle
concepts.definition: A simple duct-blown wind instrument giving one or a few shrill tones, used for signals and as percussion.

concepts.label: Samba whistle
concepts.definition: A loud whistle with several tones used by the director of a samba percussion section to give cues.

concepts.label: Xiao
concepts.definition: A Chinese end-blown bamboo flute with a soft, breathy tone.

concepts.label: Brass
concepts.definition: A family of wind instruments sounded by vibrating the player's lips into a mouthpiece, regardless of the material used for the body.

concepts.label: Trumpet
concepts.definition: A high-register brass instrument, commonly using three valves to change the effective tube length and pitch.

concepts.label: Muted trumpet
concepts.definition: A trumpet sound altered by a mute placed in or near the bell, changing tone color, projection, and sometimes dynamic response.

concepts.label: Flugelhorn
concepts.definition: A valved brass instrument similar in range to the trumpet but with a more conical bore and typically mellower tone.

concepts.label: Cornet
concepts.definition: A valved brass instrument related to the trumpet, generally with a more conical bore and compact tubing.

concepts.label: Trombone
concepts.definition: A brass instrument commonly using a movable slide to change pitch, enabling continuous glissandos and flexible intonation.

concepts.label: French horn
concepts.definition: A brass instrument with coiled tubing and a flared bell, known for a rounded tone and wide range.

concepts.label: Tuba
concepts.definition: A large, low-register valved brass instrument that often provides bass support in orchestras and wind ensembles.

concepts.label: Sousaphone
concepts.definition: A tuba built to wrap around the player's body, with a large forward-facing bell, used in marching bands and New Orleans brass bands.

concepts.label: Euphonium
concepts.definition: A conical valved brass instrument in the tenor-baritone range, prominent in brass bands and wind bands.

concepts.label: Horn section
concepts.definition: A coordinated group of brass and sometimes woodwind players providing riffs, chords, accents, or melodic lines.

concepts.label: Bugle
concepts.definition: A valveless brass instrument that plays only natural harmonics, used for military calls and in drum and bugle corps.

concepts.label: Mellophone
concepts.definition: A forward-belled valved brass instrument in the horn range, used in marching bands and drum corps.

concepts.label: Keyboards
concepts.definition: Instruments played through a keyboard, encompassing acoustic, electromechanical, and electronic sound-production systems.

concepts.label: Piano
concepts.definition: A keyboard instrument in which hammers strike strings, allowing changes in loudness through the player's touch.

concepts.label: Grand piano
concepts.definition: A piano with strings and soundboard arranged horizontally, typically offering a responsive action and broad dynamic range.

concepts.label: Honky-tonk piano
concepts.definition: A piano sound associated with honky-tonk settings, often featuring bright attack and slightly detuned or deliberately rough tuning.

concepts.label: Prepared piano
concepts.definition: A piano whose sound is altered by placing objects on or between its strings, creating unusual pitches, timbres, and percussion-like effects.

concepts.label: Electric grand piano
concepts.definition: A grand-piano-like instrument with strings and hammers whose sound is captured by pickups, made portable for stage use.
concepts.note: A piano with strings and pickups; not an electric piano with tines or reeds.

concepts.label: Electric piano
concepts.definition: A keyboard instrument whose struck mechanical elements are amplified electrically, distinct from a purely electronic or sampled digital piano.

concepts.label: Rhodes piano
concepts.definition: An electromechanical electric piano using hammer-struck metal tines and pickups, known for a bell-like attack and warm sustain.

concepts.label: Wurlitzer electric piano
concepts.definition: An electromechanical electric piano using struck reeds, known for a compact design and a tone that can become gritty under strong playing.

concepts.label: Organ
concepts.definition: A keyboard instrument producing sustained tones through pipes, reeds, electronic circuits, or digital sound generation.

concepts.label: Hammond organ
concepts.definition: An electric organ originally using rotating tonewheels, commonly associated with drawbar tone shaping and rotary-speaker effects.

concepts.label: Pipe organ
concepts.definition: A keyboard instrument that directs pressurized air into sets of pipes, selected through stops to combine contrasting tone colors.

concepts.label: Combo organ
concepts.definition: A portable electronic organ associated with popular music, especially 1960s rock, using transistor-based sound generation.
concepts.note: Transistor organ of the 1960s.

concepts.label: Barrel organ
concepts.definition: A mechanical organ in which a hand-turned pinned barrel plays the tunes, typical of street music.

concepts.label: Harpsichord
concepts.definition: A keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked mechanically, producing a clear attack with limited touch-controlled dynamics.

concepts.label: Clavinet
concepts.definition: An amplified keyboard instrument with hammer-struck strings, known for its sharp, percussive sound in funk and related styles.

concepts.label: Accordion
concepts.definition: A bellows-driven free-reed instrument with keys or buttons for melody and, in many designs, bass and chord accompaniment.

concepts.label: Diatonic button accordion
concepts.definition: An accordion with buttons instead of a piano keyboard, in which each button usually gives one note when the bellows open and another when they close.
concepts.note: Each button gives a different note on the push and on the pull.

concepts.label: Bandoneon
concepts.definition: A button-operated free-reed instrument of the concertina family, strongly associated with Argentine and Uruguayan tango.

concepts.label: Concertina
concepts.definition: A compact bellows-driven free-reed instrument with buttons at both ends, made in several systems and traditions.

concepts.label: Harmonium
concepts.definition: A free-reed keyboard instrument supplied with air by bellows, widely used in South Asian and other musical traditions.

concepts.label: Celesta
concepts.definition: A keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates, producing a soft, bell-like tone.

concepts.label: Mellotron
concepts.definition: A keyboard instrument that plays prerecorded sounds from strips of magnetic tape, historically used for orchestral and choral textures.

concepts.label: Melodica
concepts.definition: A small free-reed keyboard instrument sounded by blowing air through a mouthpiece or tube.

concepts.label: Toy piano
concepts.definition: A small keyboard instrument that commonly strikes metal rods rather than strings, producing a bright, delicate tone.

concepts.label: Electronic instruments
concepts.definition: Instruments that generate or substantially produce musical sound through electronic circuitry or digital processing.

concepts.label: Synthesizer
concepts.definition: An electronic instrument that creates and shapes sound through oscillators or other sound sources, modulation, and processing.

concepts.label: Analog synthesizer
concepts.definition: A synthesizer using analog electronic circuits to generate and shape sound, often through oscillators, filters, and amplifiers.

concepts.label: String synthesizer
concepts.definition: An electronic keyboard, mainly of the 1970s and 1980s, built to imitate an orchestral string section, usually with an ensemble or chorus effect.
concepts.note: Instrument, not the general sound of a string pad.

concepts.label: Modular synthesizer
concepts.definition: A synthesizer assembled from separate sound-generating and processing modules connected through patch cables or equivalent routing.

concepts.label: FM synthesis
concepts.definition: A synthesis method in which one oscillator modulates the frequency of another, producing complex spectra and distinctive bell-like or metallic timbres.
concepts.note: The method; for the instrument use Yamaha DX7.

concepts.label: Yamaha DX7
concepts.definition: A digital synthesizer released by Yamaha in 1983 that made FM synthesis widespread, known for electric piano, bell and bass sounds.

concepts.label: Synth pad
concepts.definition: A sustained synthesizer sound used to provide harmonic support or atmosphere, often with a soft attack and slowly evolving texture.

concepts.label: Synth lead
concepts.definition: A synthesizer sound used for a foreground melody, hook, or solo, usually designed for clear musical presence.

concepts.label: Supersaw
concepts.definition: A synthesizer timbre created by combining multiple detuned sawtooth waves for a wide, dense sound associated with trance and other dance styles.
concepts.note: Stacked detuned saw waves; trance and EDM.

concepts.label: Arpeggiator
concepts.definition: A device or function that converts held notes into a repeating sequence of individual pitches according to a selected pattern.

concepts.label: Synth bass
concepts.definition: A low-register sound generated by a synthesizer, used for bass lines, sustained foundations, or rhythmic low-frequency patterns.

concepts.label: Acid bass
concepts.definition: A resonant, often sliding bass sound associated with the Roland TB-303 and acid house or techno.
concepts.note: TB-303 line with resonance and glides.

concepts.label: Reese bass
concepts.definition: A dense, moving bass timbre created through detuned oscillators and processing, widely used in jungle and drum and bass.
concepts.note: Detuned saw bass; drum and bass.

concepts.label: Reverse bass
concepts.definition: A bass sound with a swelling or reversed-envelope character, often placed between kick hits in hardstyle-oriented production.
concepts.note: Bass with a reversed envelope between kicks; hardstyle.

concepts.label: Wobble bass
concepts.definition: A bass sound whose tone or level changes rhythmically through modulation, especially filter movement controlled by a low-frequency oscillator.
concepts.note: LFO-modulated bass; dubstep.

concepts.label: Hoover sound
concepts.definition: A thick, animated synthesizer timbre associated with early rave music, typically combining detuned waves, pitch movement, and modulation.
concepts.note: 90s rave synth sound.

concepts.label: Rave stab
concepts.definition: A short, emphatic synthesized or sampled chord used as a rhythmic accent in rave-oriented electronic music.
concepts.note: Short, aggressive synth chord.

concepts.label: Step sequencer
concepts.definition: A sequencing device or interface that stores musical events in discrete steps and plays them in a repeating pattern.
concepts.note: Grid-programmed patterns that loop.

concepts.label: Keytar
concepts.definition: A keyboard, usually a synthesizer or controller, worn with a shoulder strap and played standing like a guitar.

concepts.label: Wind synthesizer
concepts.definition: An electronic controller played like a wind instrument, whose breath and key sensors drive a synthesizer.

concepts.label: Guitar synthesizer
concepts.definition: A system that converts the playing of a guitar into control signals for a synthesizer, usually through a pickup with one output per string.

concepts.label: Drum machine
concepts.definition: An electronic instrument or software system that programs and plays percussion patterns using synthesized or sampled sounds.

concepts.label: Roland TR-808
concepts.definition: A Roland drum machine introduced in 1980, known for synthesized percussion and a resonant kick sound that also functions as bass in many productions.
concepts.note: Drum machine whose long kick doubles as bass.

concepts.label: Roland TR-909
concepts.definition: A Roland drum machine combining synthesized and sampled percussion, influential in house, techno, and other dance music.
concepts.note: Drum machine of house and techno.

concepts.label: LinnDrum
concepts.definition: A sampled drum machine associated with 1980s popular music, using digitally stored recordings of acoustic percussion.
concepts.note: Drum machine of 80s pop.

concepts.label: Sampler
concepts.definition: An electronic instrument that records, stores, and plays back sound samples, often allowing pitch changes, editing, and keyboard control.

concepts.label: Theremin
concepts.definition: An electronic instrument played without physical contact, using hand position near antennas to control pitch and volume.

concepts.label: Vocoder
concepts.definition: A system that uses the spectral characteristics of one sound, often speech, to shape another sound such as a synthesizer tone.

concepts.label: Talk box
concepts.definition: A device that sends an instrument's sound into the performer's mouth through a tube, allowing mouth shapes to alter its timbre.

concepts.label: Sound chip
concepts.definition: A sound-generating integrated circuit associated with computers or game consoles, producing characteristic electronic tones and noise.
concepts.note: Sounds of vintage consoles and home computers.

concepts.label: Log drum
concepts.definition: Here, a synthesized percussive bass timbre associated with amapiano, distinct from the acoustic wooden instruments also called log drums.
concepts.note: Percussive bass sound of amapiano.

concepts.label: Turntables
concepts.definition: Record players used as performance instruments for playback manipulation, scratching, mixing, and rhythmic recombination.

concepts.label: Percussion
concepts.definition: Instruments sounded through striking, shaking, scraping, or related actions, providing rhythm, pitch, or sound color.

concepts.label: Drum kit
concepts.definition: A collection of drums and cymbals arranged for one performer, commonly including kick, snare, toms, and hi-hat.

concepts.label: Kick drum
concepts.definition: A low-pitched drum in a kit, usually struck by a pedal-operated beater to provide the main bass pulse.

concepts.label: Snare drum
concepts.definition: A drum fitted with vibrating snares against a head, producing a sharp, rattling attack.

concepts.label: Hi-hat
concepts.definition: A pair of cymbals mounted on a stand and controlled by a foot pedal, played closed, open, or through pedal action.

concepts.label: Cymbals
concepts.definition: Metal percussion instruments producing ringing or noisy sounds when struck or brought together, with many sizes and functions.

concepts.label: Toms
concepts.definition: Drums without snares, commonly used in a kit for fills, melodic contours, and contrasting rhythmic accents.

concepts.label: Electronic drums
concepts.definition: A percussion system using pads or triggers to control synthesized or sampled drum sounds.

concepts.label: Hand percussion
concepts.definition: Percussion instruments played directly with the hands or held while shaken, scraped, or struck.

concepts.label: Congas
concepts.definition: Tall, usually single-headed hand drums associated with Afro-Cuban music, played in contrasting tones and interlocking patterns.

concepts.label: Quinto
concepts.definition: The smallest and highest conga drum, which improvises in rumba.

concepts.label: Bongos
concepts.definition: A joined pair of small, single-headed drums, commonly played with the fingers and hands in Cuban and other styles.

concepts.label: Timbales
concepts.definition: A pair of shallow, metal-shell drums played with sticks, often combined with cowbells and used in Latin dance ensembles.

concepts.label: Cajón
concepts.definition: A box-shaped percussion instrument sounded by striking its surfaces, originally associated with Afro-Peruvian traditions and later widely adopted elsewhere.

concepts.label: Djembe
concepts.definition: A rope-tuned goblet-shaped hand drum associated with West African traditions, capable of distinct bass, tone, and slap sounds.

concepts.label: Darbuka
