concepts.definition: A goblet-shaped hand drum used in Middle Eastern, North African, and neighboring traditions, producing contrasting bass and high tones.

concepts.label: Frame drum
concepts.definition: A drum whose shell is relatively shallow compared with the diameter of its head, found in many musical traditions.
concepts.note: General term; use the narrower terms for specific frame drums.

concepts.label: Bodhrán
concepts.definition: An Irish frame drum held upright and struck with a double-ended stick, the other hand pressing the skin to change pitch and tone.

concepts.label: Pandeiro
concepts.definition: A Brazilian frame drum with metal jingles, played with the hand and fingers in samba, choro and capoeira.

concepts.label: Tamborim
concepts.definition: A small Brazilian frame drum without jingles, struck with a stick in samba.

concepts.label: Daf
concepts.definition: A large frame drum of Iran, Kurdistan and neighboring regions, often with metal rings inside the frame.

concepts.label: Riq
concepts.definition: An Arabic frame drum with pairs of metal jingles, used in classical ensembles.

concepts.label: Bendir
concepts.definition: A North African frame drum without jingles, usually with a snare string under the skin that adds a buzz.

concepts.label: Doira
concepts.definition: A Central Asian frame drum with metal rings inside the frame, used in Uzbek and Tajik music.

concepts.label: Tabla
concepts.definition: A pair of tuned hand drums used particularly in Hindustani music, with contrasting sizes and a wide vocabulary of strokes.

concepts.label: Mridangam
concepts.definition: A double-headed barrel drum central to Carnatic music, played with the hands to articulate complex rhythmic patterns.
concepts.note: Double-headed drum of Carnatic music.

concepts.label: Talking drum
concepts.definition: A pressure-controlled drum whose pitch can change during playing, allowing contours that can resemble speech in several West African traditions.

concepts.label: Tambourine
concepts.definition: A handheld frame instrument with jingles, often also fitted with a drumhead, sounded by striking, shaking, or rubbing.

concepts.label: Shaker
concepts.definition: A percussion instrument that produces rhythmic sound through shaking, usually by moving loose material inside a container.

concepts.label: Maracas
concepts.definition: A pair of rattles, traditionally gourds filled with seeds, shaken in Latin American and Caribbean music.

concepts.label: Ganzá
concepts.definition: A Brazilian tube shaker of metal or woven material filled with seeds or beads.

concepts.label: Güiro
concepts.definition: A ridged scraper associated with Latin American music, sounded by drawing a stick across its grooves.

concepts.label: Güira
concepts.definition: A metal scraper with a perforated or ridged surface, played with a stiff brush, characteristic of Dominican merengue and bachata.
concepts.note: Metal scraper played with a wire brush; not the gourd güiro.

concepts.label: Cowbell
concepts.definition: A metal percussion instrument struck with a stick, often providing repeated timekeeping or syncopated patterns.

concepts.label: Claves
concepts.definition: A pair of wooden sticks struck together to produce a clear, penetrating click, commonly used to articulate clave patterns.

concepts.label: Castanets
concepts.definition: A pair or set of small concave percussion pieces clicked together, particularly associated with Spanish dance traditions.

concepts.label: Handclaps
concepts.definition: Percussive sounds produced by striking the hands together, used for rhythmic accents, accompaniment, or communal participation.

concepts.label: Finger snaps
concepts.definition: Percussive clicks created by snapping a finger against the palm, often used as light rhythmic accompaniment.

concepts.label: Cuíca
concepts.definition: A Brazilian friction drum whose internal rod is rubbed to vary its distinctive squealing pitch and timbre.

concepts.label: Surdo
concepts.definition: A large, low-pitched Brazilian drum used to anchor the pulse in samba and related ensembles.

concepts.label: Caixa
concepts.definition: The Brazilian snare drum, played with sticks in samba and maracatu.

concepts.label: Repinique
concepts.definition: A high-pitched two-headed Brazilian drum whose player leads calls and breaks in a samba percussion section.

concepts.label: Atabaque
concepts.definition: A tall Afro-Brazilian hand drum, used in Candomblé ceremonies and in capoeira.

concepts.label: Dholak
concepts.definition: A two-headed barrel drum of South Asia played with the hands, used in folk music, qawwali, bhangra and film songs.

concepts.label: Ghatam
concepts.definition: A clay pot played with the fingers, palms and wrists as a percussion instrument in South Indian classical music.

concepts.label: Sabar
concepts.definition: A Senegalese drum played with one hand and one stick, central to Wolof music and mbalax.

concepts.label: Wood block
concepts.definition: A hollow block of wood struck with a stick or mallet, giving a short, dry, high-pitched knock.

concepts.label: Agogô
concepts.definition: A double or multiple bell of West African origin, struck with a stick, used in samba and Afro-Brazilian music.

concepts.label: Shekere
concepts.definition: A dried gourd covered with a net of beads or seeds, shaken and struck, from West Africa.

concepts.label: Udu
concepts.definition: A clay pot drum of Nigerian origin with a side hole, played with the hands to produce deep, liquid tones.

concepts.label: Washboard
concepts.definition: A ridged surface used as a percussion instrument by scraping or tapping, often with thimbles or other small implements.

concepts.label: Afoxé
concepts.definition: A Brazilian gourd rattle covered with a net of beads, shaken or twisted against the palm.

concepts.label: Barrel drum
concepts.definition: A drum with a barrel-shaped body, played with the hands or sticks, such as the drums of Puerto Rican bomba.

concepts.label: Buk
concepts.definition: A Korean barrel drum played with a stick and the hand, the accompaniment of pansori and part of pungmul.

concepts.label: Caxixi
concepts.definition: A small Brazilian woven basket rattle, often played together with the berimbau.

concepts.label: Clapsticks
concepts.definition: A pair of wooden sticks struck together to keep the beat in Aboriginal Australian song.

concepts.label: Friction drum
concepts.definition: A drum sounded by rubbing a stick or cord attached to the skin, producing a grunting or moaning tone.

concepts.label: Janggu
concepts.definition: A Korean hourglass drum with two heads of different pitch, played with a stick and a mallet or the hand.

concepts.label: Kartal
concepts.definition: Indian wooden clappers with small jingles, played in pairs in devotional music.

concepts.label: Kkwaenggwari
concepts.definition: A small flat Korean brass gong struck with a wooden mallet; it leads the pungmul percussion band.

concepts.label: Kotsuzumi
concepts.definition: A Japanese hourglass drum held on the shoulder, whose pitch is changed by squeezing the cords; used in noh and kabuki.

concepts.label: Qraqeb
concepts.definition: Pairs of large iron castanets played in triplet patterns in Moroccan Gnawa music.

concepts.label: Kudüm
concepts.definition: A pair of small Turkish kettledrums that keep the rhythmic cycle in Ottoman classical and Sufi music.

concepts.label: Madal
concepts.definition: A Nepali two-headed cylindrical hand drum, the basic rhythm instrument of Nepali folk music.

concepts.label: Pakhawaj
concepts.definition: A two-headed barrel drum of North India, the accompanying drum of dhrupad and Odissi music.

concepts.label: Phách
concepts.definition: Vietnamese bamboo or wooden clappers that keep the beat in ca trù and other traditional music.

concepts.label: Quijada
concepts.definition: A donkey or horse jawbone whose loose teeth rattle when struck or scraped, used in Afro-Latin American music.

concepts.label: Ratchet
concepts.definition: A noise-maker in which a cogwheel turns against a wooden tongue, producing a loud clatter.

concepts.label: Tombak
concepts.definition: The Persian goblet drum, played with the fingers in classical and popular music.

concepts.label: Ōtsuzumi
concepts.definition: A Japanese hourglass drum held on the hip, struck for a dry, cracking sound in noh and kabuki.

concepts.label: Large drums
concepts.definition: A practical grouping of larger drums used for strong low-frequency pulses, ensemble support, or ceremonial impact.

concepts.label: Dhol
concepts.definition: A family of double-headed drums used across South Asian traditions, often played with sticks for dance and ceremonial music.
concepts.note: Double-headed drum from Punjab.

concepts.label: Taiko
concepts.definition: A Japanese term for drums and, in common international usage, ensembles or performance traditions built around them.

concepts.label: Shime-daiko
concepts.definition: A small high-pitched Japanese drum with rope-tensioned heads, used in festivals, kabuki and folk music.

concepts.label: Timpani
concepts.definition: Tuned kettle drums whose pitches can be adjusted through tension mechanisms, commonly used in orchestral music.

concepts.label: Bombo legüero
concepts.definition: An Argentine bass drum with a wooden shell and hide heads, struck on the head and the rim in Andean and Argentine folk music.

concepts.label: Dunun
concepts.definition: West African cylindrical bass drums played with sticks, often with an attached bell, that form the base of djembe ensembles.

concepts.label: Alfaia
concepts.definition: A large rope-tuned Brazilian bass drum played with sticks, the core of maracatu.

concepts.label: Garifuna drums
concepts.definition: The paired hardwood drums of Garifuna music, the lead primero and the bass segunda, played with the hands.

concepts.label: Zabumba
concepts.definition: A Brazilian bass drum struck with a mallet on top and a thin stick underneath, the drum of forró and baião.

concepts.label: Pitched percussion
concepts.definition: Percussion instruments designed to produce recognizable musical pitches, allowing melodies, harmonies, or tuned accompaniment.

concepts.label: Marimba
concepts.definition: A tuned percussion instrument with wooden bars and resonators, played with mallets for melody, harmony, or rhythmic patterns.

concepts.label: Vibraphone
concepts.definition: A mallet instrument with metal bars, sustain control, and rotating resonator mechanisms that can create a pulsating effect.

concepts.label: Xylophone
concepts.definition: A tuned percussion instrument with wooden bars, typically producing a bright, short sound when struck with mallets.

concepts.label: Ranat ek
concepts.definition: A Thai boat-shaped xylophone with twenty-one bars that leads ensemble melodies with fast octaves.

concepts.label: Glockenspiel
concepts.definition: A tuned percussion instrument with metal bars, producing a bright, bell-like tone in a high register.

concepts.label: Tubular bells
concepts.definition: A set of tuned metal tubes struck to produce bell-like pitches, commonly used in orchestral and ensemble music.

concepts.label: Steelpan
concepts.definition: A tuned percussion instrument developed in Trinidad and Tobago, formed from a steel surface divided into distinct pitch areas.

concepts.label: Kalimba
concepts.definition: A lamellophone with tuned metal tongues plucked by the thumbs or fingers, related to several African instrument traditions.

concepts.label: Handpan
concepts.definition: A tuned steel percussion instrument played with the hands, producing resonant notes from shaped tone fields around its surface.

concepts.label: Gamelan
concepts.definition: An Indonesian ensemble tradition centered on tuned percussion such as metallophones and gongs, often joined by drums, strings, or voices.
concepts.note: Ensemble of metallophones and gongs from Java and Bali.

concepts.label: Triangle
concepts.definition: A metal percussion instrument bent into a triangular shape and struck with a beater to produce a bright ringing sound.

concepts.label: Gong
concepts.definition: A metal percussion instrument, often circular, that produces resonant tones or complex sound masses when struck.

concepts.label: Balafon
concepts.definition: A West African wooden-bar percussion instrument, commonly using gourd resonators and played with mallets.
concepts.note: African xylophone with gourd resonators.

concepts.label: Gong chime
concepts.definition: A set of tuned bossed gongs laid in a row or circle and struck with mallets to play melodies, typical of Southeast Asia.

concepts.label: Khong wong yai
concepts.definition: A Thai circle of sixteen tuned gongs that plays the main melody of the piphat ensemble.

concepts.label: Marímbula
concepts.definition: A large Caribbean box with plucked metal tongues that supplies the bass in son, mento and related music.

concepts.label: Mark tree
concepts.definition: A row of hanging metal rods of graded length that sound a shimmering cascade when swept with the hand or a stick.

concepts.label: Jaw harp
concepts.definition: A small instrument with a flexible tongue held against the open mouth and plucked, the mouth shaping its overtones.

concepts.label: Anvil
concepts.definition: A blacksmith's anvil, or a steel bar substituting for one, struck as a percussion instrument.
concepts.note: Struck as a percussion instrument.

concepts.label: Bell
concepts.definition: A hollow, usually metal idiophone struck or shaken to ring, from handbells and cowbell-like timeline bells to church bells.

concepts.label: Gankogui
concepts.definition: A West African double iron bell that plays the timeline pattern in Ewe drumming.

concepts.label: Handbell
concepts.definition: A bell with a handle, rung by swinging, played in tuned sets by handbell choirs.

concepts.label: Ensembles
concepts.definition: A group of performers making music together, ranging from small chamber groups to large orchestras or bands.

concepts.label: Orchestra
concepts.definition: A large instrumental ensemble typically combining strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion, though its makeup varies by repertory.

concepts.label: Chamber orchestra
concepts.definition: A smaller orchestra intended for chamber-scale repertory or performance spaces, usually with fewer players per part.

concepts.label: String quartet
concepts.definition: An ensemble of two violins, viola, and cello, or a composition written for this combination.

concepts.label: Big band
concepts.definition: A large jazz ensemble typically organized into saxophone, trumpet, trombone, and rhythm sections.

concepts.label: Brass band
concepts.definition: An ensemble centered on brass instruments, often with percussion; instrumentation and repertory vary among regional traditions.

concepts.label: Power trio
concepts.definition: A three-piece rock ensemble typically consisting of guitar, bass, and drums, with one or more members also singing.
concepts.note: Guitar, bass and drums.

concepts.label: Mariachi ensemble
concepts.definition: A Mexican ensemble tradition commonly combining violins, trumpets, guitars, vihuela, and guitarrón, with instrumentation varying historically.
concepts.note: Trumpets, violins, guitarrón and vihuela.

concepts.label: Samba bateria
concepts.definition: The percussion section of a samba school, combining surdos, snare drums, repiniques, tamborims, cuícas and other instruments.
concepts.note: Percussion section of a samba school.

concepts.label: Tamburica orchestra
concepts.definition: An ensemble of long-necked plucked tamburica instruments of different sizes, traditional in Croatia, Serbia and Hungary.

concepts.label: Rock band
concepts.definition: An ensemble performing rock-oriented music, commonly built around guitars, bass, drums, and vocals, sometimes with keyboards or other instruments.

concepts.label: Solo performer
concepts.definition: A musician performing alone, possibly singing, playing an instrument, or combining several musical roles.

concepts.label: Cobla
concepts.definition: The Catalan wind band of eleven players (flabiol and tabor, tibles, tenoras, brass and double bass) that accompanies the sardana.

concepts.label: Guitar techniques
concepts.definition: A method of playing guitar that shapes note production, articulation, rhythm, pitch, or tone color.

concepts.label: Palm muting
concepts.definition: A guitar or bass technique in which the picking-hand palm lightly damps the strings near the bridge, shortening and darkening their sound.
concepts.note: Strings damped with the palm for a dry, percussive sound.

concepts.label: Chugging
concepts.definition: Repeated low-register, often palm-muted guitar figures that create a heavy, percussive pulse.
concepts.note: Repeated low muted power chords.

concepts.label: Djent riffing
concepts.definition: Guitar riffing characterized by tightly muted, low-register attacks and syncopated accents, often played on extended-range instruments.
concepts.note: Syncopated muted riffs on very low strings with a metallic attack.

concepts.label: Tremolo picking
concepts.definition: Rapid repeated picking of a note or small figure, usually through alternating strokes, to create a sustained or intensely articulated sound.
concepts.note: Very fast alternate picking on one note; black metal, surf.

concepts.label: Alternate picking
concepts.definition: A picking technique that alternates downstrokes and upstrokes for successive notes.

concepts.label: Sweep picking
concepts.definition: A picking technique that moves across several strings in one coordinated stroke while the fretting hand articulates separate notes.
concepts.note: Fast arpeggios with a sweeping pick stroke.

concepts.label: Tapping
concepts.definition: A string-instrument technique that sounds notes by striking the fingerboard with fingers rather than plucking every note.
concepts.note: Notes sounded by the picking hand on the fretboard.

concepts.label: Legato (guitar)
concepts.definition: A guitar approach connecting notes through hammer-ons, pull-offs, slides, or related techniques to reduce separate picked attacks.
concepts.note: Slurred notes without picking.

concepts.label: Hammer-on
concepts.definition: A guitar technique in which a fretting finger strikes the string firmly enough to sound a higher note without picking it.
concepts.note: A fretting finger strikes the string to sound a higher note without picking.

concepts.label: Pull-off
concepts.definition: A guitar technique in which a fretting finger is pulled off the string, plucking it slightly to sound a lower note.
concepts.note: A fretting finger pulls off the string to sound a lower note without picking.

concepts.label: String bending
concepts.definition: A technique that raises a string's pitch by pushing or pulling it sideways, allowing expressive transitions and inflections.
concepts.note: Stretching the string to raise the pitch.

concepts.label: Whammy bar
concepts.definition: A guitar vibrato-system lever used to change string tension, enabling pitch dips, rises, and vibrato effects.

concepts.label: Pinch harmonics
concepts.definition: A technique that combines a picked attack with brief finger or thumb contact to emphasize a high harmonic of the string.
concepts.note: High harmonics produced with the pick; metal.

concepts.label: Natural harmonics
concepts.definition: Tones produced by lightly touching a vibrating string at a nodal point, suppressing some partials and emphasizing a harmonic.

concepts.label: Slide guitar
concepts.definition: A guitar technique using a slide or bar against the strings to create continuous pitch movement and sustained notes.
concepts.note: Notes slid with a tube along the strings.

concepts.label: Fingerpicking
concepts.definition: A guitar or related string technique using individual fingers to pluck separate strings or coordinated patterns.
concepts.note: Playing with the fingers.

concepts.label: Travis picking
concepts.definition: A fingerpicking style in which the thumb maintains an alternating bass pattern while other fingers play melody or accompaniment.
concepts.note: Alternating thumb bass with finger-played melody.

concepts.label: Strumming
concepts.definition: Sounding several strings in a coordinated sweeping motion, usually to articulate chords or rhythmic accompaniment.

concepts.label: Rasgueado
concepts.definition: A flamenco guitar strumming technique using coordinated finger strokes to create rapid, strongly articulated chord patterns.
concepts.note: Fan-like strums of flamenco guitar.

concepts.label: Picado
concepts.definition: A flamenco guitar technique for clear, rapid single-note passages, usually played with alternating fingers.
concepts.note: Fast scales plucked with alternating fingers.

concepts.label: Chicken picking
concepts.definition: A country-oriented picking approach using crisp attacks, muted notes, and plucked accents to create a clucking, percussive sound.
concepts.note: Clucky, staccato country picking.

concepts.label: Funk guitar scratching
concepts.definition: Percussive guitar strumming across muted strings, used to create rhythmic subdivisions and syncopated texture.
concepts.note: Percussive strumming on muted strings.

concepts.label: Skank guitar
concepts.definition: Short offbeat guitar chords that provide rhythmic punctuation in ska, reggae, and related styles.
concepts.note: Short offbeat chord; reggae and ska.

concepts.label: Jangle guitar
concepts.definition: A bright, ringing guitar sound produced through clear attacks, sustained open strings, and often arpeggiated chords or twelve-string instruments.
concepts.note: Bright arpeggios of open chords; jangle pop.

concepts.label: Shred guitar
concepts.definition: A virtuosic guitar approach emphasizing speed, precise articulation, and demanding techniques such as rapid picking, legato, and tapping.
concepts.note: Virtuosic high-speed solos.

concepts.label: Neoclassical shred
concepts.definition: Virtuosic guitar playing drawing on classical-style sequences, arpeggios, and harmonic-minor or related pitch resources.
concepts.note: Shred based on Baroque scales and arpeggios.

concepts.label: Guitar feedback
concepts.definition: A sustained or growing sound created when an amplified guitar signal re-enters the pickup or instrument and forms a feedback loop.
concepts.note: Controlled amplifier feedback.

concepts.label: Drop tuning
concepts.definition: A guitar or bass tuning in which the lowest string is lowered relative to the other strings, changing low-register range and chord shapes.
concepts.note: Tuning with the lowest string lowered.

concepts.label: Open tuning
concepts.definition: A tuning in which the unstopped strings form a chord, facilitating drones, slide playing, and alternative chord voicings.
concepts.note: Tuning that forms a chord on open strings.

concepts.label: Chord melody
concepts.definition: A guitar arrangement or playing style that combines a melody with its supporting chords in the same part.
concepts.note: Harmonized melody on a single guitar.

concepts.label: Bass techniques
concepts.definition: A method of playing bass that shapes articulation, pitch, rhythmic function, or tone color.

concepts.label: Slap bass
concepts.definition: A bass technique combining struck strings and often plucked pops for a bright, percussive sound; execution differs between electric and upright bass.
concepts.note: Thumb slap and string pop.

concepts.label: Walking bass
concepts.definition: A moving bass line, commonly in regular quarter notes, that outlines harmonies while connecting them smoothly.
concepts.note: Quarter-note bass outlining the chords; jazz.

concepts.label: Octave bass
concepts.definition: A bass pattern alternating or combining pitches one octave apart, often used to create rhythmic drive in dance-oriented music.
concepts.note: Bass alternating octaves; disco.

concepts.label: Picked bass
concepts.definition: Bass playing with a plectrum, often producing a clear attack and consistent articulation.

concepts.label: Bass glides
concepts.definition: Continuous pitch movement between bass notes, produced by sliding along a string or using electronic pitch glide.
concepts.note: Pitch glides in the bass.

concepts.label: Keyboard techniques
concepts.definition: A method of keyboard playing that shapes accompaniment, voicing, articulation, coordination, or melodic delivery.

concepts.label: Stride piano
concepts.definition: A jazz piano style in which the left hand alternates low bass notes with higher chords while the right hand plays melody or improvisation.
concepts.note: Left hand alternating bass and chord; early jazz.

concepts.label: Boogie-woogie bass
concepts.definition: A repeated left-hand piano bass pattern supporting a blues-based groove, often using rolling or broken-chord figures.
concepts.note: Left-hand blues figures in ostinato.

concepts.label: Montuno
concepts.definition: A repeating, syncopated accompaniment figure, especially on piano, associated with Cuban music and salsa.
concepts.note: Syncopated, repeated piano figure in salsa.

concepts.label: Block chords
concepts.definition: A harmonization technique in which several notes move together rhythmically, often placing a chord beneath each melody note.

concepts.label: Piano glissando
concepts.definition: A rapid sweep across successive piano keys, creating a continuous-looking gesture from discrete pitches.

concepts.label: Bowed-string techniques
concepts.definition: A method of playing bowed string instruments that changes articulation, timbre, sustain, or the number of sounding strings.

concepts.label: Pizzicato
concepts.definition: A technique in which strings normally played with a bow are plucked instead.
concepts.note: Strings plucked with the fingers.

concepts.label: String tremolo
concepts.definition: Rapid repeated bow strokes on a pitch or figure, producing a sustained, agitated, or shimmering string texture.
concepts.note: Very fast bowed repetition.

concepts.label: Staccato strings
concepts.definition: Short, separated notes on bowed string instruments, produced through bowing and release techniques appropriate to the passage.
concepts.note: The short articulation; for the bouncing bow stroke use Spiccato.

concepts.label: Spiccato
concepts.definition: A bow stroke in which the bow bounces off the string, producing short, light notes.
concepts.note: Bow stroke that bounces off the string.

concepts.label: Legato strings
concepts.definition: Smoothly connected notes on bowed string instruments, with transitions shaped to minimize audible separation.

concepts.label: Col legno
concepts.definition: A string technique using the wooden part of the bow against the strings, either striking them or drawing it across them.
concepts.note: Striking with the wood of the bow.

concepts.label: Double stops
concepts.definition: The simultaneous sounding of two strings on a bowed string instrument, creating intervals or supporting harmonies.

concepts.label: String swells
concepts.definition: Sustained string sounds that gradually increase or decrease in intensity, often through bow pressure, speed, or ensemble dynamics.

concepts.label: Wind techniques
concepts.definition: A performance method on wind instruments that shapes breath, articulation, pitch, resonance, or tone color.

concepts.label: Saxophone growl
concepts.definition: A rough saxophone effect often produced by vocalizing while playing, causing the sung tone to interact with the instrument's sound.
concepts.note: Saxophone with voice added; rough sound.

concepts.label: Flutter-tonguing
concepts.definition: A wind-instrument technique using rapid tongue or throat vibration to create a rolling or fluttering tone.

concepts.label: Brass stabs
concepts.definition: Short, emphatic brass notes or chords used to punctuate a groove, phrase, or transition.
concepts.note: Short hits from the horn section.

concepts.label: Falls and doits
concepts.definition: Brass gestures that trail downward as falls or upward as doits, usually at the end of a note and with flexible pitch contour.
concepts.note: Brass glissandos at the end of a note.

concepts.label: Circular breathing
concepts.definition: A wind-playing technique that maintains airflow to an instrument while inhaling through the nose using air stored in the cheeks.

concepts.label: DJ techniques
concepts.definition: A method of manipulating recordings during performance, including mixing, scratching, and rhythmic recombination.

concepts.label: Scratching
concepts.definition: The rhythmic manipulation of a record or equivalent digital playback by moving it backward and forward to reshape the sound.
concepts.note: Moving the vinyl to create rhythms.

concepts.label: Beat juggling
concepts.definition: A DJ technique that rearranges short recorded passages through repeated playback and switching, often between two copies of a record.

concepts.label: Recording aesthetic
concepts.definition: The overall sonic character of a recording, shaped by production choices, technology, performance, and intentional imperfections.
concepts.note: Overall character of the recorded sound.

concepts.label: Lo-fi
concepts.definition: A recording aesthetic that retains or emphasizes imperfections such as noise, limited bandwidth, distortion, or rough performance texture.
concepts.note: Deliberately imperfect, saturated or muffled sound.

concepts.label: Vinyl crackle
concepts.definition: Short clicks and crackling noise associated with record playback, sometimes added deliberately as a textural effect.

concepts.label: Tape hiss
concepts.definition: Broadband background noise associated with magnetic-tape recording, sometimes retained or recreated for atmosphere.

concepts.label: Bedroom production
concepts.definition: Music production carried out in a small personal space, often using accessible recording tools and an informal working process.

concepts.label: Polished production
concepts.definition: A polished production aesthetic emphasizing controlled recording, editing, balance, and clarity; it does not require a particular loudness or dynamic range.
concepts.note: Clean, compressed, competitive sound.

concepts.label: Raw production
concepts.definition: A recording aesthetic that preserves directness, performance irregularities, and relatively limited editing or processing.
concepts.note: Direct sound with little editing.

concepts.label: Live recording
concepts.definition: A recording made during a performance or simultaneous ensemble session, retaining aspects of real-time interaction and the performance setting.
concepts.note: Concert or live-in-studio take.

concepts.label: Analog warmth
concepts.definition: A subjective descriptor for tonal qualities associated with some analog equipment, often involving gentle saturation, rounded transients, or spectral coloration.
concepts.note: The perceived quality; for the process use Tape saturation.

concepts.label: Wall of sound
concepts.definition: A dense, layered production sound associated with Phil Spector's method and, more broadly, heavily blended arrangements or effects-rich textures.
concepts.note: Dense layers with heavy reverb; Phil Spector, shoegaze.

concepts.label: Bass-heavy mix
concepts.definition: A mix in which low-frequency elements are particularly prominent relative to the rest of the spectrum.
concepts.note: Bass dominates the mix.

concepts.label: Sub-bass
concepts.definition: Very low-frequency sound, commonly below about 60 Hz, perceived as deep bass and often felt physically as well as heard.
concepts.note: Low frequencies below ~60 Hz, whatever instrument or synth produces them.

concepts.label: Dry mix
concepts.definition: A mix using little audible reverberation or echo, creating a close, relatively direct presentation of sounds.
concepts.note: Little reverb, close sound.

concepts.label: Field recording
concepts.definition: The recording of sounds outside a conventional studio, including environments, everyday activity, and music in its original setting.
concepts.note: Environmental sounds recorded outside the studio.

concepts.label: Dynamics processing
concepts.definition: Audio processing that changes signal level over time, including compression, limiting, expansion, and gating.

concepts.label: Compression
concepts.definition: Processing that reduces differences between louder and quieter signal levels according to selected threshold, ratio, and timing settings.
concepts.note: Reducing dynamic range.

concepts.label: Sidechain compression
concepts.definition: Compression whose gain reduction is controlled by a separate signal or filtered detector input, often used to make one part yield to another.
concepts.note: The signal ducks with each kick.

concepts.label: Limiting
concepts.definition: Dynamic processing that strongly restricts peaks above a threshold, commonly used to control maximum output level.

concepts.label: Spatial effects
concepts.definition: Audio effects that create or modify perceived distance, room ambience, direction, or width.

concepts.label: Reverb
concepts.definition: The dense persistence of sound after its source stops, caused naturally by reflections or recreated through audio processing.

concepts.label: Hall reverb
concepts.definition: A reverberation sound modeled on a large hall, typically providing an extended decay and spacious ambience.

concepts.label: Plate reverb
concepts.definition: A reverberation effect created by vibrating a metal plate or digitally modeling that behavior, often producing a smooth, dense tail.

concepts.label: Spring reverb
concepts.definition: A reverberation effect created through vibrating springs or their simulation, known for a distinctive metallic or splashy character.
concepts.note: Metallic amplifier reverb; surf.

concepts.label: Gated reverb
concepts.definition: A reverberation effect abruptly shortened by a gate or similar processing, producing a large ambience followed by a sharp cutoff.
concepts.note: Abruptly cut-off reverb; 80s drums.

concepts.label: Shimmer reverb
concepts.definition: A reverberation effect combined with pitch-shifted feedback, often adding sustained upper-octave layers to the decay.
concepts.note: Reverb with an added upper octave.

concepts.label: Delay
concepts.definition: An effect that repeats a sound after a chosen time interval, with timing and feedback controlling the rhythmic or spatial result.
concepts.note: Repetitions of the signal.

concepts.label: Tape delay
concepts.definition: A delay effect produced by recording and replaying sound on moving magnetic tape, or by digitally modeling its characteristic behavior.

concepts.label: Slapback echo
concepts.definition: A short, usually single audible echo that thickens a sound without creating a long chain of repetitions.
concepts.note: Single short echo; rockabilly.

concepts.label: Dub echo
concepts.definition: Echo processing associated with dub, often using live changes in feedback, timing, and filtering to transform a recording.
concepts.note: Feedback delays manipulated live.

concepts.label: Panning
concepts.definition: The placement or movement of a sound between channels to create an apparent position within the stereo image.

concepts.label: Modulation effects
concepts.definition: Effects that vary a sound parameter over time, often cyclically, to create motion, doubling, or changing tone color.

concepts.label: Chorus effect
concepts.definition: An effect that combines a signal with slightly delayed and pitch-varied copies to suggest multiple performers or a broader sound.
concepts.note: Slightly detuned doubling.

concepts.label: Flanger
concepts.definition: An effect that mixes a signal with a very short, changing delay, producing moving comb-filter peaks and notches.

concepts.label: Phaser
concepts.definition: An effect that combines a signal with phase-shifted copies, creating moving frequency notches and a sweeping timbre.

concepts.label: Tremolo effect
concepts.definition: A periodic variation in sound level, distinct from vibrato, which varies pitch.
concepts.note: Periodic volume variation.

concepts.label: Rotary speaker
concepts.definition: The sound of a loudspeaker cabinet with a rotating horn and drum, or a simulation of it, which produces shifting volume, pitch and space; strongly associated with the Hammond organ.
concepts.note: The effect of a rotating speaker cabinet, or its simulation; classic with the Hammond organ.

concepts.label: Distortion
concepts.definition: A deliberate or incidental alteration of a signal that changes its waveform and often adds harmonics through clipping or saturation.
concepts.note: Clipping that adds harmonics.

concepts.label: Overdrive
concepts.definition: A form of distortion associated with driving an amplifier or modeled circuit beyond its clean range, often producing comparatively soft clipping.
concepts.note: Mild tube saturation.

concepts.label: Tape saturation
concepts.definition: The soft compression and harmonic distortion that occur when analog tape is recorded at high levels, or a digital emulation of it.
concepts.note: Soft compression and harmonic distortion from driving analog tape, or its emulation.

concepts.label: Fuzz
concepts.definition: A strong distortion effect that produces a thick, buzzy, or sharply clipped tone, commonly used with electric guitar.
concepts.note: Harsh, square-wave distortion.

concepts.label: Bitcrusher
concepts.definition: A digital effect that reduces bit depth, sample rate, or both to introduce quantization noise and other coarse digital artifacts.
concepts.note: Digital resolution reduction.

concepts.label: Distorted vocals
concepts.definition: Vocals processed or captured with deliberate clipping, saturation, or other distortion to add grit, density, or aggression.

concepts.label: Filters
concepts.definition: Audio effects that reshape the frequency spectrum by emphasizing, attenuating, or removing selected frequency regions.

concepts.label: Filter sweep
concepts.definition: A gradual change in a filter's cutoff or other setting, creating a moving change in brightness or spectral emphasis.
concepts.note: Gradual opening or closing of a filter.

concepts.label: Resonant filter
concepts.definition: A filter that emphasizes frequencies near its cutoff, creating a pronounced peak that can sound ringing or sharply colored.
concepts.note: Filter with pronounced resonance; acid.

concepts.label: Wah-wah
concepts.definition: A filter-based effect whose moving frequency emphasis produces a vowel-like sound, often controlled by a foot pedal.
concepts.note: Foot-swept filter pedal.

concepts.label: Envelope filter
concepts.definition: A filter whose behavior responds to the changing level or envelope of the input signal, producing touch-sensitive tonal movement.

concepts.label: Pitch effects
concepts.definition: Audio processes that alter, correct, or multiply pitch, including pitch shifting, harmonization, and pitch correction.

concepts.label: Auto-Tune
concepts.definition: Pitch-correction processing associated with the Auto-Tune product and similar tools, used subtly for tuning or audibly as a stylized effect.
concepts.note: Audible pitch correction used as an effect.

concepts.label: Pitch shifting
concepts.definition: Processing that moves a sound to a different pitch, ideally without requiring a corresponding change in duration.

concepts.label: Pitched-up vocals
concepts.definition: Vocals shifted to a higher pitch for a lighter, smaller, or stylized sound; the resulting timbre depends on formant treatment.

concepts.label: Slowed and reverb
concepts.definition: A production treatment that slows a recording and adds reverberation, often lowering pitch when playback speed is reduced; it is distinct from chopped-and-screwed editing.
concepts.note: Slowed-down version with reverb; or the chopped and screwed technique.

concepts.label: Harmonizer
concepts.definition: A pitch-processing effect that adds one or more shifted copies of a sound to create harmonies or thicker textures.

concepts.label: Octaver
concepts.definition: A pitch effect that adds a copy of a sound one or more octaves above or below the original.

concepts.label: Time manipulation
concepts.definition: Audio processes that change playback direction, timing, repetition, or duration to reshape musical material.

concepts.label: Reverse
concepts.definition: Playback of recorded sound backward, reversing its attacks, decays, and internal sequence.
concepts.note: Recording played backwards.

concepts.label: Stutter edit
concepts.definition: Rapid repetition of a short audio fragment, producing a chopped or interrupted rhythmic effect.
concepts.note: Choppy repetitions of a fragment.

concepts.label: Tape stop
concepts.definition: An effect that slows playback toward a halt, often lowering pitch and imitating a stopping tape machine or turntable.
concepts.note: Simulated tape slowdown to a halt.

concepts.label: Time-stretching
concepts.definition: Processing that changes an audio recording's duration, ideally while preserving its original pitch.

concepts.label: Sampling
concepts.definition: The use of recorded sound fragments as musical material, often through editing, repetition, pitch changes, or recombination.
concepts.note: Reusing recorded fragments.

concepts.label: Loop
concepts.definition: A recorded or programmed musical passage repeated cyclically to create accompaniment, texture, or a structural foundation.
concepts.note: Fragment repeated cyclically.

concepts.label: Vocal chops
concepts.definition: Short vocal fragments edited and rearranged as rhythmic or melodic material, often treated like an instrument.
concepts.note: Chopped vocal fragments used as an instrument.

concepts.label: Sample flip
concepts.definition: A creative transformation of a sample through editing, rearrangement, pitch changes, or processing to give it a new musical role.
concepts.note: Creative transformation of a recognizable sample.

concepts.label: Sound design
concepts.definition: The deliberate creation and shaping of sounds, including timbres, textures, effects, and transitions that serve a musical or dramatic purpose.
concepts.note: Non-musical sound elements with a structural role.

concepts.label: Riser
concepts.definition: A transition sound that increases in pitch, intensity, density, or brightness to build anticipation.
concepts.note: Rising sound that builds tension.

concepts.label: Downlifter
concepts.definition: A transition sound that falls in pitch, intensity, or brightness, often following a climax or introducing a new section.
concepts.note: Falling sound after a climax.

concepts.label: Impact
concepts.definition: A short, forceful sound used to emphasize a section entry, edit, or dramatic event, often combining low-frequency and noisy layers.
concepts.note: Low hit at the start of a section.

concepts.label: Braam
concepts.definition: A loud, low, often brass-like or heavily processed cinematic sound used for dramatic emphasis in trailers and soundtrack-oriented music.
concepts.note: Distorted low brass from trailers.

concepts.label: Sub drop
concepts.definition: A low-frequency sound that descends in pitch, often used to mark a transition or add weight to a section.
concepts.note: Pitch drop in the sub-bass.

concepts.label: Ambient texture
concepts.definition: A sustained or evolving background sound that establishes space, atmosphere, or continuity rather than a clear foreground melody.

concepts.label: Era aesthetic
concepts.definition: A production descriptor referring to sonic traits associated with a historical period, while recognizing that each period contains many different styles.
concepts.note: Production traits associated with a decade.

concepts.label: 1950s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 1950s recording traits, such as prominent live ensembles, restrained editing, and period-specific studio ambience.

concepts.label: 1960s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 1960s recording traits, such as tape-based tracking, distinctive room or plate reverberation, and experimental studio layering.

concepts.label: 1970s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 1970s recording traits, such as analog multitracking, distinctive drum-room sounds, and warm electric instrumentation.

concepts.label: 1980s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 1980s traits, often including drum machines, synthesizers, digital reverberation, and strongly processed drums.

concepts.label: 1990s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 1990s traits, such as sample-based production, prominent alternative-rock guitars, or early digital processing, depending on style.

concepts.label: 2000s sound
concepts.definition: A production aesthetic referencing selected 2000s traits, often involving computer-based editing, tightly controlled dynamics, and increasingly digital production workflows.

concepts.label: Modern sound
concepts.definition: A contemporary production aesthetic associated with current recording, editing, and mixing practices; its meaning changes over time and across styles.

concepts.label: Dynamics
concepts.definition: The relative loudness and intensity of musical sounds, including contrasts and changes within a phrase or piece.
concepts.note: Management of volume and intensity.

concepts.label: Soft dynamics
concepts.definition: Playing or singing at a comparatively quiet level, with its expressive effect depending on timbre, context, and contrast.

concepts.label: Loud dynamics
concepts.definition: Playing or singing at a comparatively strong level, often creating emphasis or intensity without necessarily implying distortion.

concepts.label: Crescendo
concepts.definition: A gradual increase in musical loudness or intensity over a passage.
concepts.note: Gradual increase in intensity.

concepts.label: Decrescendo
concepts.definition: A gradual decrease in musical loudness or intensity over a passage.

concepts.label: Sforzando
concepts.definition: A sudden, forceful emphasis on a note or chord, usually understood in relation to the surrounding dynamic level.
concepts.note: Sudden, strong accent.

concepts.label: Dynamic contrast
concepts.definition: A marked difference in loudness or intensity between musical passages, parts, or successive events.
concepts.note: Alternating soft and explosive sections.

concepts.label: Slow build
concepts.definition: A gradual accumulation of intensity across an extended passage or piece, achieved through dynamics, layering, pacing, or harmonic tension.
concepts.note: Intensity that grows throughout the piece.

concepts.label: Articulation
concepts.definition: The way notes begin, end, and connect, shaping their attack, duration, separation, and expressive character.
concepts.note: How notes are attacked and connected.

concepts.label: Staccato
concepts.definition: An articulation in which notes are shortened and separated from one another.
concepts.note: Short, separated notes.

concepts.label: Legato
concepts.definition: An articulation in which successive notes are smoothly connected with minimal separation.
concepts.note: Notes connected without a break.

concepts.label: Marcato
concepts.definition: An articulation indicating clear emphasis or marked attack, giving notes a more pronounced presence.

concepts.label: Tenuto
concepts.definition: A marking indicating that a note should be sustained for its full value, sometimes with additional emphasis depending on context.

concepts.label: Lyrical devices
concepts.definition: A writing technique that shapes the sound, structure, imagery, or meaning of song lyrics.
concepts.note: Lyric-writing devices.

concepts.label: Rhyme scheme
concepts.definition: The organized pattern of rhyming line endings in lyrics or verse, often represented by letters such as ABAB or AABB.
concepts.note: Distribution of rhymes (AABB, ABAB…).

concepts.label: Internal rhyme
concepts.definition: Rhyme occurring within a line or between internal positions in neighboring lines rather than only at line endings.
concepts.note: Rhymes within the same line.

concepts.label: Multisyllabic rhyme
concepts.definition: A rhyme extending across more than one syllable, often used to create elaborate sound patterns in rap and other lyrics.
concepts.note: Chained multi-syllable rhymes; rap.

concepts.label: Assonance
concepts.definition: The repetition of similar vowel sounds in nearby words, creating sonic cohesion without requiring full rhyme.

concepts.label: Repetition
concepts.definition: The deliberate recurrence of words, lines, or phrases to emphasize an idea, establish rhythm, or create a memorable hook.

concepts.label: Storytelling
concepts.definition: Lyrics that develop events, characters, or a narrative perspective, whether through a clear sequence or fragmented scenes.
concepts.note: The lyrics tell a story with characters.

concepts.label: Punchline
concepts.definition: A concluding or emphatic line that delivers a joke, surprise, verbal twist, or pointed comparison, especially in rap.
concepts.note: Witty closing line; rap.

concepts.label: Double entendre
concepts.definition: A word or phrase that supports two interpretations, often combining an ordinary meaning with a humorous, suggestive, or hidden one.

concepts.label: Title drop
concepts.definition: The inclusion of a work's title within its lyrics, often at a memorable or structurally prominent moment.
concepts.note: The title appears in the hook.

concepts.label: Vocables
concepts.definition: Sung syllables without a conventional lexical meaning, used for melody, rhythm, expression, or vocal texture.
concepts.note: Meaningless sung syllables.

concepts.label: Onomatopoeia
concepts.definition: The use of words or vocal sounds that imitate the noises they describe.

concepts.label: Code-switching
concepts.definition: The alternation between languages or language varieties within lyrics or vocal performance.
concepts.note: Switching languages within the lyrics.

concepts.label: Protest lyrics
concepts.definition: Lyrics that criticize, challenge, or mobilize around social or political conditions, often expressing demands or collective concerns.
concepts.note: Social or political lyrics.

concepts.label: Confessional lyrics
concepts.definition: Lyrics presenting intimate personal feelings, experiences, or self-examination, often through a first-person perspective.
concepts.note: Intimate first-person lyrics.

concepts.label: Abstract lyrics
concepts.definition: Lyrics that emphasize imagery, ambiguity, association, or sound rather than a straightforward narrative or explicit literal message.

concepts.label: Instrumental
concepts.definition: A musical piece or recording presented without a principal sung or spoken vocal part, though incidental nonverbal vocal sounds may sometimes appear.
concepts.note: Piece without vocals.

concepts.label: Mood
concepts.definition: A descriptor of a music passage's perceived emotional or expressive character, shaped by sound, context, and individual interpretation.
concepts.note: Affective descriptors. Not technical devices, but music-generation prompts rely on them heavily.

concepts.label: Bright and happy
concepts.definition: A perceived cheerful or light musical character, often suggested by buoyant rhythm, clear timbres, or lively phrasing rather than any single technical feature.

concepts.label: Uplifting
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as encouraging, hopeful, or elevating, often supported by rising energy and a sense of release.

concepts.label: Melancholic
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as wistful, sorrowful, or gently sad, without requiring a particular key or tempo.

concepts.label: Nostalgic
concepts.definition: A musical character that evokes memory, longing, or a sense of the past through style, timbre, melody, or personal association.

concepts.label: Dark
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as shadowed, somber, or heavy, shaped by timbre, harmony, register, and context.

concepts.label: Ominous
concepts.definition: A musical character that suggests approaching danger or unease, often through tension, unresolved motion, or restrained intensity.

concepts.label: Aggressive
concepts.definition: A musical character emphasizing force, confrontation, or abrasive energy through performance, rhythm, dynamics, or timbre.

concepts.label: Energetic
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as active and vigorous, supported by rhythmic drive, strong attacks, or sustained intensity.

concepts.label: Chill
concepts.definition: A relaxed, low-pressure musical character, often using restrained dynamics, unhurried pacing, and soft or spacious textures.

concepts.label: Dreamy
concepts.definition: A floating or imagined musical character, often suggested by blurred attacks, sustained textures, spacious effects, or gentle melodic movement.

concepts.label: Hypnotic
concepts.definition: A musical character that encourages sustained absorption through repetition, steady pulse, gradual change, or immersive texture.

concepts.label: Epic
concepts.definition: A musical character suggesting large scale, grandeur, or dramatic stakes, often created through broad gestures and accumulating intensity.

concepts.label: Anthemic
concepts.definition: A bold, memorable musical character suited to collective participation, often using strong hooks and emphatic recurring phrases.
concepts.note: Made to be sung by a crowd.

concepts.label: Romantic
concepts.definition: A musical character associated with affection, intimacy, or emotional longing, distinct from the historical Romantic period.

concepts.label: Sensual
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as physically intimate or seductive, often through smooth phrasing, tactile timbres, or a relaxed groove.

concepts.label: Playful
concepts.definition: A light, mischievous, or humorous musical character, often created through unexpected gestures, buoyant rhythms, or contrasting sounds.

concepts.label: Theatrical
concepts.definition: A musical character emphasizing dramatic presentation, heightened expression, or staged contrasts.

concepts.label: Mysterious
concepts.definition: A musical character that suggests uncertainty or hidden meaning through ambiguous harmony, unusual timbres, or incomplete resolution.

concepts.label: Introspective
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as inward-looking or reflective, often supported by restrained delivery and space for detailed expression.

concepts.label: Triumphant
concepts.definition: A musical character suggesting achievement, victory, or confident arrival, often using strong accents and a sense of resolution.

concepts.label: Spiritual
concepts.definition: A musical character associated with contemplation, transcendence, or sacred experience, without implying one particular religious tradition.

concepts.label: Groovy
concepts.definition: A musical character centered on an engaging rhythmic feel that invites bodily movement, often through coordinated accents and timing.

concepts.label: Raw
concepts.definition: A musical character perceived as unpolished, direct, or emotionally exposed, often retaining rough timbres and performance irregularities.
